# Combo29 integration validation

Repository: `couns0538-sketch/dwqww`. Integration branch: `integrate/combo29-fixes`.
Base: `lock/combo29-20261110` at `16833ecc03b425586f91f4c8834dea8807bf4c22`.
Tested engine head: `66ffa41903f793b3ae5483fac9be32055b025b58`.

All work ran in the attached cloud VM under `/workspace/work`. No command ran on the owner's PC.
The source boundary is the remote-ref snapshot taken at **2026-11-14 05:00:24 UTC** (2026-11-13 21:00:24 America/Los_Angeles).
Only the six grok47 branches in that snapshot were considered. Later branch arrivals or updates were not imported.

## Result

Four source changes were reapplied as four separate linear commits, with the release build, six required node checks, and cumulative ASan/UBSan regressions completed before each commit. No engine source was patched to make a failing test pass. A final documentation commit adds only this file.

- Per-step release builds, all six node checks, and cumulative ASan/UBSan tests: **PASS after each of t1, t3, t6, and t8**.
- Final TSan run: **200/200 depth-12 searches completed, zero findings, exit 0, empty stderr**.
- Final fastchess run: **400/400 games; integration 200 wins, 200 losses, 0 draws; zero crashes, illegal moves, disconnects, or aborted games; exit 0**.

These are correctness, crash, and legality observations. No Elo or speed conclusion is drawn. Raw engine output includes its own time and NPS fields; they are reproduced solely to preserve the actual output.

The t8 change adds the source branch's `NnueFile` capability. It is included as the explicitly named 7/8 task, not described as a repair to an existing file loader. No additional loader features were authored here. Its only new UCI option advertises `NnueFile type string default <empty>`; all required node checks and the final runs leave it at that default, using the built-in network.

t1 and t3 additionally passed byte-for-byte comparisons of their source patch and staged patch. t6 and t8 apply on previously changed files; stable patch-ID comparisons ignore shifted hunk locations and index hashes. Source changes are confined to `forge-combo29/src`, `forge-combo29/include`, and the corresponding `tests_t1`, `tests_t3`, `tests_t6`, `tests_t8` directories. All compiled binaries, generated network files, fastchess sources/builds, and temporary test drivers remain outside the committed changes. The temporary in-repository release build directory was moved outside the repository after validation.

## Choices and exclusions

- **1 versus 2:** select t1. No t2 branch existed in the starting snapshot.
- **3 versus 4:** select t3. The frozen t4 tip was `2a52e7f45bcb3d7da7946fceb219061e2d2a0d4a`. Besides clock parsing, t4 changes parsing of depth, mate, and movestogo. t3 is narrower and its second source commit handles malformed double signs and overflow followed by junk.
- **7 versus 8:** select t8. No t7 branch existed in the starting snapshot.
- **t5 omitted:** `grok47/t5-krk-mate` at `1c3a5e0a11043c0d91d683f40691dd386a5158e4` clears all worker history tables before every search and disables all helper-thread TT stores and generation refreshes. Its tests demand matching single-thread and two-thread move/score results and matching results with and without a prior search. Those equalities do not establish a chess correctness requirement. The patch changes ordinary repeated-search and multithread behavior, while the benchmark already clears history and can conceal that change. It was rejected at source review rather than narrowed or patched. Its tests were not run as an added fix.
- All source branch `REPORT_tN.md` files were omitted because they fall outside the allowed changed paths.
- No changes were taken from branches absent from the starting snapshot, including later Grok work. A later read-only remote audit observed t5 advancing to `321fe8f8cb1a1b1321b47c1a49530c3e0a8e09d1` and a new `grok47/t10-multipv` branch. Neither later revision was fetched or integrated; the t5 review here concerns only its starting commit.
- This task did not write, merge, rebase, or delete any other remote branch or tag. Fetches of source commits were by frozen SHA. Local lock references and the inherited local tag remained at their starting commits.

## Per-step checks (a–c)

The cloud CPU exposes AVX-512 and BMI2. The requested unmodified release command was therefore used without the portable override:

```bash
cmake -S forge-combo29 -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release && cmake --build build -j
```

CMake was 3.31.6, GCC was 14.2.0. The lock CMake configuration supplies `-march=x86-64-v4`, strict floating-point flags, and its original feature definitions. No CMake source changes were made.

Every node-check process was fresh, issued `uci`, explicitly set Threads 1, Hash 16, OwnBook false, and left all other options at their defaults until the two requested UseNNUE=false benches.

| Tree tested | NNUE on: bench 11 / 13 / 16 | NNUE off: bench 11 / 13 | Startpos perft 5 | Release build | Cumulative ASan/UBSan |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Unchanged lock | 312866 / 862329 / 3024920 | 375354 / 907205 | 4865609 | PASS | Not required before adding a fix |
| + t1 | 312866 / 862329 / 3024920 | 375354 / 907205 | 4865609 | PASS | t1 PASS |
| + t3 | 312866 / 862329 / 3024920 | 375354 / 907205 | 4865609 | PASS | t1 and t3 PASS |
| + t6 | 312866 / 862329 / 3024920 | 375354 / 907205 | 4865609 | PASS | t1, t3, t6 PASS |
| + t8 | 312866 / 862329 / 3024920 | 375354 / 907205 | 4865609 | PASS | t1, t3, t6, t8 PASS |

Sanitizer builds instrument the complete engine with `-fsanitize=address,undefined -g -fno-omit-frame-pointer -fno-sanitize-recover=all`. Regression programs link the current instrumented engine objects with the same lock definitions and ISA/FP options. The standalone parser and network converter are also instrumented. ASan leak detection and halt-on-error are enabled; UBSan halt-on-error and stack traces are enabled. No sanitizer suppression was used. No ASan, UBSan, or LeakSanitizer report appeared in the successful runs.

Coverage:
- t1: source regression reports 68 losing captures, a legal best move, and a clean exit.
- t3: source parser regression plus all seven cases in `clock_commands.txt`, awaiting each bestmove. Both large clocks remained searching at 150 ms and were then stopped. The +80 case was nonzero; negative and malformed clocks completed promptly.
- t6: source regression checks move/score agreement with the completed depth across node budgets spanning best-move changes, in startpos and a rook ending.
- t8: source converter, source loader regression, and actual UCI output matching all lines in `expected_uci.txt`. Checks cover equivalent converted weights, changed weights, built-in restoration, invalid magic/version/dimensions/length, and a missing file.

### Failures and corrected validation invocations

All failed validation commands and their original outputs are preserved below; none was hidden or replaced.

1. The first t1 output checker mistakenly extracted field 8 (`time`) instead of field 7 (the node count). Its checker exit status was 1 even though all six actual printed counts matched. The corrected checker examined the same saved output and passed. This changed only the validation command.
2. The first t8 converter compile command omitted `-march=x86-64-v4` while passing the lock's PEXT definition. The existing header correctly rejected it with `FORGE_SPD_SLIDER_PEXT=1 needs BMI2`. The corrected invocation used the same ISA and FP flags as the engine. The source regression programs and engine were unchanged.
3. An exploratory `git show` for `tests_t8/FORMAT.txt` failed because that file does not exist. The actual tree was listed; its text expectations file is `expected_uci.txt`.
4. Initial environment/tool availability probes and the tooling transcript include unsuccessful lookups. Git/GCC/Make and sanitizer runtimes were present; CMake was provisioned under the cloud work directory from a checksum-verified upstream distribution. The user's suggested sudo package installation was not needed.

## Final threaded and game checks (d–e)

### d. ThreadSanitizer

The final engine was built separately with GCC ThreadSanitizer. With Threads 2, Hash 16, OwnBook false, and remaining options at defaults, the driver ran all eight benchmark FENs 25 times each, awaiting each search. All 200 searches emitted depth 12 and one bestmove. TT/history were retained between searches. Engine exit status was 0; raw stderr was 0 bytes. **Every TSan finding: none.** No suppressions were used. The build and all commands, protocol traffic, and result checks are reproduced in the TSan transcript.

TSan executable SHA256: `1d76179ec392eb2569cacc20f5f12acdb876aa1449f961256d4a5d1fe74c3753`.

### e. fastchess crash and legality check

Built fastchess from upstream commit `3d7a4db2493fc85a05ef010fd7e13a3884667aa2` without source modifications. The run used `-rounds 200 -games 2 -recover -concurrency 2`, no `-openings`, and `-each nodes=20000 option.Threads=1 option.Hash=16 option.OwnBook=false`. All other engine options remained at defaults. The full exact command is in the transcript.

**Result from integration perspective: 200 wins, 200 losses, 0 draws. All 400 games completed; fastchess exit status 0.** All game results were normal checkmates. The 400 PGNs and 400 completion events agreed; all 63,600 move events were legal. There were **0 crashes, 0 illegal moves, 0 disconnects, 0 aborted games, 0 abnormal terminations, and no trace error/fatal findings**. Every actual UCI search command was `go nodes 20000`, 31,800 per engine. Both engine hashes were unchanged after the match.

Executable SHA256 values:

- Integration: `e7670190216dd4060c460207e8c070103f3cf8ba9fedde27576aa3304e19631b`.
- Unchanged lock: `1371770e2ad61aa2fe3c038acc7da3912da5d64c9cb1dcc5e4668221fb3226f6`. This binary was built and copied before any fix was applied.

Fastchess emitted two opening warnings: no opening book specified, and unknown opening format 2. Both explicitly say the games use the starting position, as intended. It also emitted one final rating line despite `-ratinginterval 0`. That line is preserved only as raw program output; it is not interpreted as strength evidence. These were the only console warnings; there were no game incidents.

The full console and all audit commands/output are embedded below. Supporting PGN, event records, and the optional 257 MB engine debug trace remain in the cloud work directory, outside the repository; their sizes and SHA256 hashes appear in the audit transcript. No generated binaries or archives were committed.

## Limits of verification

The patch comparisons prove that the committed source changes are the selected source patches, and the node checks prove equality for the requested signatures. They do not prove equality for every position, option, compiler, or schedule. Intentional corrected behavior is different (for example, fixed-node bestmove selection and wide-clock parsing).
The excluded t5 changes and branches absent at the starting snapshot were not integrated or validated.
Only this cloud Linux/GCC/x86-64-v4 configuration was executed; no claim is made about Windows builds, other architectures, strength, or performance.
The full source-review transcripts sometimes print historical source-branch reports; those quoted reports are not treated as fresh test results. Fresh evidence is in the explicitly labeled validation runs below.
All requested checks (a–e) completed in this environment. No required check remains unexecuted. Passing these finite checks does not establish a universal absence of bugs or races.

`````text
# Cloud build tooling transcript

All setup writes were under `/workspace/work`. Compiler and sanitizer runtimes already present. The initial inspection below is transcribed from its real tool output; the unchanged apt wrapper was reread to preserve its long text exactly.

## Command

total 44
drwx------ 2 agent agent  4096 Nov 13 21:00 .

#!/bin/sh
# applied-artifactory-apt-wrapper
set -e

ARTIFACTORY_APT_ROOT="https://applied-jfrog-cache.gateway.ci-1.internal.api.openai.org/artifactory"
PRESERVE_APT_SOURCES="1"
ARTIFACTORY_APT_LIST_PATH="/etc/apt/applied-artifactory/sources.list"
UBUNTU_AMD64_ARCHIVE_REPO="ubuntu-live-amd64-archive"
UBUNTU_AMD64_SECURITY_REPO="ubuntu-live-amd64-security"
UBUNTU_ARM64_REPO="ubuntu-live-arm64"
DEBIAN_ARCHIVE_REPO="debian-live-archive"
DEBIAN_SECURITY_REPO="debian-live-security"
ARTIFACTORY_APT_OVERRIDE_MARKER="/etc/apt/applied-artifactory/.applied-artifactory"
ARTIFACTORY_APT_SOURCE_DIR="/etc/apt/applied-artifactory/sources.list.d"
ARTIFACTORY_APT_INHERITED_SOURCES_PATH="/etc/apt/applied-artifactory/inherited-source-checksums"
ARTIFACTORY_APT_CONFIG_PATH="/etc/apt/apt.conf.d/99-applied-build-sources"
ARTIFACTORY_APT_CONFIG_FILE="/etc/apt/applied-artifactory/apt.conf"
REAL_APT_GET="${REAL_APT_GET:-/usr/bin/apt-get}"
REAL_APT="${REAL_APT:-/usr/bin/apt}"
APT_SOURCES_LIST_PATH="${APT_SOURCES_LIST_PATH:-/etc/apt/sources.list}"
APT_SOURCES_DIR_PATH="${APT_SOURCES_DIR_PATH:-/etc/apt/sources.list.d}"

artifactory_apt_override_is_active() {
  [ -f "$ARTIFACTORY_APT_OVERRIDE_MARKER" ] || return 1
  [ "${APT_CONFIG:-}" = "$ARTIFACTORY_APT_CONFIG_FILE" ] && return 0
  [ -L "$ARTIFACTORY_APT_CONFIG_PATH" ] &&     [ "$(readlink "$ARTIFACTORY_APT_CONFIG_PATH")" = "$ARTIFACTORY_APT_CONFIG_FILE" ]
}

if ! artifactory_apt_override_is_active; then
  case "${0##*/}" in
    apt) exec "$REAL_APT" "$@" ;;
    *) exec "$REAL_APT_GET" "$@" ;;
  esac
fi

rewrite_apt_source_file() {
  source_path="$1"
  tmp_path="$(mktemp "${source_path}.XXXXXX")" || return 1
  # Rewrite repository URI tokens only. Leave APT to interpret all other fields.
  if ! awk -v extension="${source_path##*.}" -v root="$ARTIFACTORY_APT_ROOT" \
    -v ubuntu_archive="$UBUNTU_AMD64_ARCHIVE_REPO" \
    -v ubuntu_security="$UBUNTU_AMD64_SECURITY_REPO" -v ubuntu_ports="$UBUNTU_ARM64_REPO" \
    -v debian_archive="$DEBIAN_ARCHIVE_REPO" -v debian_security="$DEBIAN_SECURITY_REPO" '
    function rewrite_root(uri, upstream, repository, n) {
      if (!match(uri, "^https?://" upstream "(/|$)")) return uri
      n = RLENGTH
      if (substr(uri, n, 1) == "/") n--
      return root "/" repository substr(uri, n + 1)
    }
    function rewrite_uri(uri) {
      uri = rewrite_root(uri, "snapshot[.]ubuntu[.]com", "ubuntu-snapshot-remote")
      uri = rewrite_root(uri, "snapshot[.]debian[.]org", "debian-snapshot-remote")
      uri = rewrite_root(uri, "([[:alnum:]-]+[.])?archive[.]ubuntu[.]com/ubuntu", ubuntu_archive)
      uri = rewrite_root(uri, "security[.]ubuntu[.]com/ubuntu", ubuntu_security)
      uri = rewrite_root(uri, "ports[.]ubuntu[.]com/ubuntu-ports", ubuntu_ports)
      uri = rewrite_root(uri, "ppa[.]launchpadcontent[.]net", "apt-ppa-launchpad-public")
      uri = rewrite_root(uri, "apt[.]postgresql[.]org/pub/repos/apt", "postgresql-pgdg-remote")
      uri = rewrite_root(uri, "(deb|security)[.]debian[.]org/debian-security", debian_security)
      return rewrite_root(uri, "(deb|httpredir|ftp([.][[:alnum:]-]+)?)[.]debian[.]org/debian", debian_archive)
    }
    function rewrite_uris(value, result, uri) {
      result = ""
      while (match(value, /[^[:space:]]+/)) {
        result = result substr(value, 1, RSTART - 1)
        uri = substr(value, RSTART, RLENGTH)
        value = substr(value, RSTART + RLENGTH)
        result = result rewrite_uri(uri)
      }
      return result value
    }
    {
      if ($0 ~ /^[[:space:]]*#/) { print; next }
      if (extension == "sources") {
        if ($0 ~ /^[^[:space:]]/ || $0 ~ /^[[:space:]]*$/)
          in_uris = tolower($0) ~ /^uris:/
        if (!in_uris) { print; next }
        prefix = ""
        value = $0
        if (match(value, /^[^[:space:]][^:]*:[[:space:]]*/)) {
          prefix = substr(value, 1, RLENGTH)
          value = substr(value, RLENGTH + 1)
        }
        print prefix rewrite_uris(value)
      } else {
        if (!match($0, /^[[:space:]]*deb(-src)?[[:space:]]+(\[[^]]*\][[:space:]]*)?/)) {
          print
          next
        }
        prefix = substr($0, 1, RLENGTH)
        value = substr($0, RLENGTH + 1)
        if (!match(value, /^[^[:space:]#]+/)) { print; next }
        uri = substr(value, 1, RLENGTH)
        suffix = substr(value, RLENGTH + 1)
        print prefix rewrite_uri(uri) suffix
      }
    }
  ' "$source_path" > "$tmp_path"; then
    rm -f "$tmp_path"
    return 1
  fi

#!/bin/sh
# applied-artifactory-apt-wrapper
set -e

ARTIFACTORY_APT_ROOT="https://applied-jfrog-cache.gateway.ci-1.internal.api.openai.org/artifactory"
PRESERVE_APT_SOURCES="1"
ARTIFACTORY_APT_LIST_PATH="/etc/apt/applied-artifactory/sources.list"
UBUNTU_AMD64_ARCHIVE_REPO="ubuntu-live-amd64-archive"
UBUNTU_AMD64_SECURITY_REPO="ubuntu-live-amd64-security"
UBUNTU_ARM64_REPO="ubuntu-live-arm64"
DEBIAN_ARCHIVE_REPO="debian-live-archive"
DEBIAN_SECURITY_REPO="debian-live-security"
ARTIFACTORY_APT_OVERRIDE_MARKER="/etc/apt/applied-artifactory/.applied-artifactory"
ARTIFACTORY_APT_SOURCE_DIR="/etc/apt/applied-artifactory/sources.list.d"
ARTIFACTORY_APT_INHERITED_SOURCES_PATH="/etc/apt/applied-artifactory/inherited-source-checksums"
ARTIFACTORY_APT_CONFIG_PATH="/etc/apt/apt.conf.d/99-applied-build-sources"
ARTIFACTORY_APT_CONFIG_FILE="/etc/apt/applied-artifactory/apt.conf"
REAL_APT_GET="${REAL_APT_GET:-/usr/bin/apt-get}"
REAL_APT="${REAL_APT:-/usr/bin/apt}"
APT_SOURCES_LIST_PATH="${APT_SOURCES_LIST_PATH:-/etc/apt/sources.list}"
APT_SOURCES_DIR_PATH="${APT_SOURCES_DIR_PATH:-/etc/apt/sources.list.d}"

artifactory_apt_override_is_active() {
  [ -f "$ARTIFACTORY_APT_OVERRIDE_MARKER" ] || return 1
  [ "${APT_CONFIG:-}" = "$ARTIFACTORY_APT_CONFIG_FILE" ] && return 0
  [ -L "$ARTIFACTORY_APT_CONFIG_PATH" ] &&     [ "$(readlink "$ARTIFACTORY_APT_CONFIG_PATH")" = "$ARTIFACTORY_APT_CONFIG_FILE" ]
}

if ! artifactory_apt_override_is_active; then
  case "${0##*/}" in
    apt) exec "$REAL_APT" "$@" ;;
    *) exec "$REAL_APT_GET" "$@" ;;
  esac
fi

rewrite_apt_source_file() {
  source_path="$1"
  tmp_path="$(mktemp "${source_path}.XXXXXX")" || return 1
  # Rewrite repository URI tokens only. Leave APT to interpret all other fields.
  if ! awk -v extension="${source_path##*.}" -v root="$ARTIFACTORY_APT_ROOT" \
    -v ubuntu_archive="$UBUNTU_AMD64_ARCHIVE_REPO" \
    -v ubuntu_security="$UBUNTU_AMD64_SECURITY_REPO" -v ubuntu_ports="$UBUNTU_ARM64_REPO" \
    -v debian_archive="$DEBIAN_ARCHIVE_REPO" -v debian_security="$DEBIAN_SECURITY_REPO" '
    function rewrite_root(uri, upstream, repository, n) {
      if (!match(uri, "^https?://" upstream "(/|$)")) return uri
      n = RLENGTH
      if (substr(uri, n, 1) == "/") n--
      return root "/" repository substr(uri, n + 1)
    }
    function rewrite_uri(uri) {
      uri = rewrite_root(uri, "snapshot[.]ubuntu[.]com", "ubuntu-snapshot-remote")
      uri = rewrite_root(uri, "snapshot[.]debian[.]org", "debian-snapshot-remote")
      uri = rewrite_root(uri, "([[:alnum:]-]+[.])?archive[.]ubuntu[.]com/ubuntu", ubuntu_archive)
      uri = rewrite_root(uri, "security[.]ubuntu[.]com/ubuntu", ubuntu_security)
      uri = rewrite_root(uri, "ports[.]ubuntu[.]com/ubuntu-ports", ubuntu_ports)
      uri = rewrite_root(uri, "ppa[.]launchpadcontent[.]net", "apt-ppa-launchpad-public")
      uri = rewrite_root(uri, "apt[.]postgresql[.]org/pub/repos/apt", "postgresql-pgdg-remote")
      uri = rewrite_root(uri, "(deb|security)[.]debian[.]org/debian-security", debian_security)
      return rewrite_root(uri, "(deb|httpredir|ftp([.][[:alnum:]-]+)?)[.]debian[.]org/debian", debian_archive)
    }
    function rewrite_uris(value, result, uri) {
      result = ""
      while (match(value, /[^[:space:]]+/)) {
        result = result substr(value, 1, RSTART - 1)
        uri = substr(value, RSTART, RLENGTH)
        value = substr(value, RSTART + RLENGTH)
        result = result rewrite_uri(uri)
      }
      return result value
    }
    {
      if ($0 ~ /^[[:space:]]*#/) { print; next }
      if (extension == "sources") {
        if ($0 ~ /^[^[:space:]]/ || $0 ~ /^[[:space:]]*$/)
          in_uris = tolower($0) ~ /^uris:/
        if (!in_uris) { print; next }
        prefix = ""
        value = $0
        if (match(value, /^[^[:space:]][^:]*:[[:space:]]*/)) {
          prefix = substr(value, 1, RLENGTH)
          value = substr(value, RLENGTH + 1)
        }
        print prefix rewrite_uris(value)
      } else {
        if (!match($0, /^[[:space:]]*deb(-src)?[[:space:]]+(\[[^]]*\][[:space:]]*)?/)) {
          print
          next
        }
        prefix = substr($0, 1, RLENGTH)
        value = substr($0, RLENGTH + 1)
        if (!match(value, /^[^[:space:]#]+/)) { print; next }
        uri = substr(value, 1, RLENGTH)
        suffix = substr(value, RLENGTH + 1)
        print prefix rewrite_uri(uri) suffix
      }
    }
  ' "$source_path" > "$tmp_path"; then
    rm -f "$tmp_path"
    return 1
  fi
  # Keep the copied source file permissions while replacing its contents.
  cat "$tmp_path" > "$source_path"
  rm -f "$tmp_path"
}

copy_added_apt_source() {
  source_path="$1"
  [ -f "$source_path" ] || return 0
  if [ "$PRESERVE_APT_SOURCES" = 1 ]; then
    # Preserve names as well as contents so APT still ignores backup files.
    if [ "$source_path" = "$APT_SOURCES_LIST_PATH" ]; then
      copied_path="$ARTIFACTORY_APT_LIST_PATH"
    else
      copied_path="$ARTIFACTORY_APT_SOURCE_DIR/${source_path##*/}"
    fi
  else
    [ -f "$ARTIFACTORY_APT_INHERITED_SOURCES_PATH" ] || return 0
    # Generated defaults replace unchanged sources inherited from the base image.
    source_checksum="$(cksum "$source_path")"
    if grep -Fqx "$source_checksum" "$ARTIFACTORY_APT_INHERITED_SOURCES_PATH"; then
      return 0
    fi
    case "$source_path" in
      *.sources) extension="sources" ;;
      *) extension="list" ;;
    esac
    copied_path="$ARTIFACTORY_APT_SOURCE_DIR/applied-third-party-${copy_number}.${extension}"
    copy_number=$((copy_number + 1))
  fi
  cp -p "$source_path" "$copied_path"
  rewrite_apt_source_file "$copied_path"
}

refresh_added_apt_sources() {
  if [ "$PRESERVE_APT_SOURCES" = 1 ]; then
    rm -f "$ARTIFACTORY_APT_LIST_PATH"
    for copied_path in "$ARTIFACTORY_APT_SOURCE_DIR"/*; do
      [ -f "$copied_path" ] || continue
      rm -f "$copied_path"
    done
  else
    for copied_path in "$ARTIFACTORY_APT_SOURCE_DIR"/applied-third-party-*; do
      [ -e "$copied_path" ] || continue
      rm -f "$copied_path"
    done
  fi

  copy_number=0
  copy_added_apt_source "$APT_SOURCES_LIST_PATH"
  for source_path in "$APT_SOURCES_DIR_PATH"/*.list "$APT_SOURCES_DIR_PATH"/*.sources; do
    copy_added_apt_source "$source_path"
  done
}

refresh_added_apt_sources
if [ "${1:-}" = "--refresh-artifactory-sources" ]; then
  exit 0
fi

case "${0##*/}" in
  apt) exec "$REAL_APT" "$@" ;;
  *) exec "$REAL_APT_GET" "$@" ;;
esac
`````

`````text
+ cat forge-combo29/CMakeLists.txt
# Forge combo29 lock: plain Linux/CMake build (GCC or Clang).
# This is NOT the Windows lock recipe (clang ThinLTO+PGO, see windows_build/).
# It builds the same source so node counts (bench pins, perft) can be checked.
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.16)
project(forge_combo29 LANGUAGES CXX)

set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
set(CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS OFF)
if(NOT CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE)
  set(CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE Release CACHE STRING "" FORCE)
endif()

# FORGE_MARCH: target CPU. The lock needs BMI2 (PEXT sliders) and AVX-512F (NNUE ZMM kernel).
set(FORGE_MARCH "x86-64-v4" CACHE STRING "value for -march (lock exe uses znver5)")
# FORGE_PORTABLE=ON drops the two ISA-bound speed switches (SLIDER_PEXT, NNUE_ZMM) so it
# builds on CPUs without AVX-512/BMI2. Use -DFORGE_MARCH=x86-64-v3 or native with it.
option(FORGE_PORTABLE "build without the PEXT/AVX-512 speed switches" OFF)

file(GLOB FORGE_SOURCES CONFIGURE_DEPENDS ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/*.cpp)
add_executable(forge ${FORGE_SOURCES})
target_include_directories(forge PRIVATE ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/include)

target_compile_definitions(forge PRIVATE
  NDEBUG
  FORGE_NNUE_HIDDEN=256
  FORGE_EXPOSE_TUNABLES=1
  FORGE_SPD_TT_NOTLS=1
  FORGE_SPD_NO_ZERO_MOVELISTS=2
  FORGE_SEARCH_SPEED2=1
  FORGE_SPD_PREFETCH_EARLY=1)
if(FORGE_PORTABLE)
  target_compile_definitions(forge PRIVATE FORGE_SPD_SLIDER_PEXT=0 FORGE_SPD_NNUE_ZMM=0)
else()
  target_compile_definitions(forge PRIVATE FORGE_SPD_SLIDER_PEXT=1 FORGE_SPD_NNUE_ZMM=1)
endif()

# Strict floating-point operation order (required for bit-exact node counts).
target_compile_options(forge PRIVATE -O3 -ffp-contract=off -fno-fast-math -march=${FORGE_MARCH})
set(THREADS_PREFER_PTHREAD_FLAG ON)
find_package(Threads REQUIRED)
target_link_libraries(forge PRIVATE Threads::Threads)
+ cat forge-combo29/README.md
# Forge combo29 (current speed lock)

Standalone Linux build of the Forge lock source. GCC 12+ or Clang 15+, CMake 3.16+, an x86-64 CPU.

```bash
cd forge-combo29
cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release && cmake --build build -j
scripts/check_pins.sh build/forge          # bench 11/13/16/20/22 net-on + net-off, then perft 5; must print "PINS MATCH combo29"
```

Manual commands (UCI on stdin): `bench 13` → `info string bench depth 13 nodes 862329 ...`;
`setoption name UseNNUE value false` then `bench 13` → `nodes 907205`; `position startpos` then `go perft 5` → `nodes 4865609`.

No AVX-512/BMI2 on the host? Configure with `-DFORGE_PORTABLE=ON -DFORGE_MARCH=x86-64-v3` (drops the PEXT and ZMM speed switches; on the box this still gave the same pins).

Rules: keep strict FP order (`-ffp-contract=off -fno-fast-math`); every engine change goes in as a default-0 switch with the lock code under `#else`; prove pins/bit-exactness first. NPS from a Linux container is not a speed result, and Elo comes only from SPRT gates on Couns's PC. See LOCK.md for hashes and where everything came from.
`````

`````text
+ cat forge-combo29/scripts/check_pins.sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Usage: scripts/check_pins.sh [path/to/forge]   (default build/forge)
# Checks the combo29 lock bench pins (net on + net off) and startpos perft 5.
set -euo pipefail
exe="${1:-build/forge}"
want_on="312866 862329 3024920 12389307 34048354"
want_off="375354 907205 2448617 13573040 24506465"
want_perft="4865609"
{
  echo "setoption name UseNNUE value true"; for d in 11 13 16 20 22; do echo "bench $d"; done
  echo "setoption name UseNNUE value false"; for d in 11 13 16 20 22; do echo "bench $d"; done
  echo "position startpos"; echo "go perft 5"; sleep 1; echo "quit"
} | "$exe" > pins_out.txt
got=$(awk '/info string bench depth/{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++) if($i=="nodes") printf "%s ", $(i+1)}' pins_out.txt)
got_on=$(echo $got | cut -d' ' -f1-5); got_off=$(echo $got | cut -d' ' -f6-10)
got_perft=$(awk '/^nodes /{print $2}' pins_out.txt | tail -1)
echo "net-on : $got_on"; echo "net-off: $got_off"; echo "perft5 : $got_perft"
if [[ "$got_on" == "$want_on" && "$got_off" == "$want_off" && "$got_perft" == "$want_perft" ]]; then
  echo "PINS MATCH combo29"; else echo "PIN MISMATCH (want on: $want_on / off: $want_off / perft5: $want_perft)"; exit 1; fi
`````

`````text
+#pragma once
+
+#include <charconv>
+#include <cstdint>
+#include <limits>
+#include <string_view>
+#include <system_error>
+
+namespace forge {
+
+// Ceiling for a parsed clock. Time allocation multiplies a clock by a small
+// tunable (at most 150), so the product has to stay inside a signed 64-bit
+// integer. 3000000000, the value that overflows a 32-bit int, is below this.
+inline constexpr std::int64_t kMaxClockMs = std::numeric_limits<std::int64_t>::max() / 256;
+
+// One UCI clock token, in milliseconds, clamped to [0, kMaxClockMs].
+// A single leading '+' is accepted. A leading '-' clamps to 0. A second sign
+// is not a number. Anything that is not a complete integer, including a
+// missing token or digits with trailing junk, is 0. A magnitude that does not
+// fit in 64 bits clamps to the ceiling only when every character was a digit.
+[[nodiscard]] inline std::int64_t parse_clock_ms(std::string_view text) {
+    if (text.empty()) return 0;
+    bool negative = false;
+    if (text.front() == '+' || text.front() == '-') {
+        negative = text.front() == '-';
+        text.remove_prefix(1);
+        if (text.empty() || text.front() == '+' || text.front() == '-') return 0;
+    }
+    std::uint64_t magnitude = 0;
+    const char* const first = text.data();
+    const char* const last = text.data() + text.size();
+    const std::from_chars_result parsed = std::from_chars(first, last, magnitude);
+    // Overflow still reports how far the digit run went. Trailing junk is 0.
+    if (parsed.ptr != last) return 0;
+    if (parsed.ec == std::errc::result_out_of_range) return negative ? 0 : kMaxClockMs;
+    if (parsed.ec != std::errc{}) return 0;
+    if (negative || magnitude > static_cast<std::uint64_t>(kMaxClockMs)) {
+        return negative ? 0 : kMaxClockMs;
+    }
+    return static_cast<std::int64_t>(magnitude);
+}
+
+} // namespace forge

@@ -0,0 +1,29 @@
+# UCI clock cases. Times are what the fixed engine does with
+# Threads 1, Hash 16, OwnBook false, Move Overhead 10 (the default).
+# The lock engine parses every one of these numbers as 0 and answers bestmove
+# in about 1 ms.
+
+# 3000000000 does not fit in a signed 32-bit int. The search must still be
+# running 150 ms later. Stop it; do not wait out the clock.
+position startpos
+go wtime 3000000000 btime 3000000000
+
+# A leading plus is 80 ms, not zero. The hard limit is 80 - overhead = 70 ms.
+position startpos
+go movetime +80
+
+# A negative clock clamps to 0. The hard limit becomes 1 ms.
+position startpos
+go movetime -5
+
+# A token that is not an integer is 0. The hard limit becomes 1 ms.
+# A second sign and overflow with trailing junk are the same, not a huge clock.
+position startpos
+go movetime abc
+go movetime +-80
+go movetime 999999999999999999999abc
+
+# Black to move uses btime. 3000000000 must not collapse to 0 just because
+# it is the black clock. wtime 1 is white's clock and is ignored here.
+position startpos moves e2e4
+go wtime 1 btime 3000000000

new file mode 100644
index 0000000..8abf514

+++ b/forge-combo29/tests_t3/clock_parse_test.cpp
@@ -0,0 +1,59 @@
+// Clock tokens used by `go wtime`, `go btime`, `go winc`, `go binc`, and
+// `go movetime`. Compile against include/:
+//   g++ -std=c++20 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -I forge-combo29/include
+//       forge-combo29/tests_t3/clock_parse_test.cpp -o /tmp/clock_parse_test
+// The lock tree has no parse_clock_ms, so this file does not build there.
+#include "forge/uci_clock.hpp"
+
+#include <cstdint>
+#include <iostream>
+#include <string_view>
+
+namespace {
+
+int failures = 0;
+
+void expect(std::string_view text, std::int64_t want, std::string_view name) {
+    const std::int64_t got = forge::parse_clock_ms(text);
+    if (got == want) return;
+    std::cerr << "FAIL " << name << " text=[" << text << "] got " << got << " want " << want << '\n';
+    ++failures;
+}
+
+} // namespace
+
+int main() {
+    expect("3000000000", 3000000000LL, "wtime above 32 bits");
+    expect("+80", 80, "movetime plus 80");
+    expect("+00080", 80, "plus and leading zeros");
+    expect("80", 80, "plain 80");
+    expect("0", 0, "zero");
+    expect("-80", 0, "negative clamps to zero");
+    expect("-0", 0, "negative zero");
+    expect("-", 0, "bare minus");
+    expect("+", 0, "bare plus");
+    expect("++80", 0, "double plus is malformed");
+    expect("+-80", 0, "plus then minus is malformed");
+    expect("-+80", 0, "minus then plus is malformed");
+    expect("+80x", 0, "trailing junk");
+    expect("9223372036854775808x", 0, "overflow with trailing junk");
+    expect("999999999999999999999abc", 0, "far overflow with trailing junk");
+    expect("12x", 0, "trailing letter");
+    expect("abc", 0, "letters");
+    expect("1.5", 0, "decimal");
+    expect("", 0, "empty");
+    expect("9223372036854775807", forge::kMaxClockMs, "int64 max clamps");
+    expect("9223372036854775808", forge::kMaxClockMs, "one past int64 max clamps");
+    expect("999999999999999999999", forge::kMaxClockMs, "far overflow clamps");
+    expect("-999999999999999999999", 0, "negative overflow clamps to zero");
+    if (3000000000LL > forge::kMaxClockMs) {
+        std::cerr << "FAIL ceiling is below 3000000000\n";
+        ++failures;
+    }
+    if (failures != 0) {
+        std::cerr << failures << " failed\n";
+        return 1;
+    }
+    std::cout << "clock_parse_test passed\n";
+    return 0;
+}

+// Ceiling for wtime/btime/winc/binc/movetime. The time formula multiplies an
+// increment by TmIncrementPercent (option max 150) and a soft limit by
+// TmHardSoftMultiple (option max 20), so the stored value has to leave
+// headroom in int64. 3000000000 ms fits.
+constexpr std::int64_t kMaxClockMs = std::numeric_limits<std::int64_t>::max() / 150;
+static_assert(kMaxClockMs > 3000000000LL);
+static_assert(kMaxClockMs / 5 + (kMaxClockMs * 150) / 100 <=
+              std::numeric_limits<std::int64_t>::max() / 20);
+
+// One go-command integer. Accepts a single leading '+', which std::from_chars
+// rejects. A value outside int64 clamps to that range. Junk or a second sign
+// yields 0, matching the old failed parse. The caller supplies 0 when the
+// number token is absent.
+std::int64_t parse_i64_token(const std::string& text) {
+    if (text.empty()) return 0;
+    const char* begin = text.data();
+    const char* end = text.data() + text.size();
+    if (*begin == '+') {
+        ++begin;
+        if (begin == end || *begin == '+' || *begin == '-') return 0;
+    }
+    std::int64_t value = 0;
+    const auto result = std::from_chars(begin, end, value);
+    if (result.ptr != end) return 0;
+    if (result.ec == std::errc::result_out_of_range) {
+        return text[0] == '-' ? std::numeric_limits<std::int64_t>::min()
+                              : std::numeric_limits<std::int64_t>::max();
+    }
+    if (result.ec != std::errc{}) return 0;
+    return value;
+}
+
+std::int64_t clamp_clock_ms(std::int64_t value) {
+    return std::clamp(value, std::int64_t{0}, kMaxClockMs);
+}

diff --git a/forge-combo29/tests_t4/check_clock.cpp b/forge-combo29/tests_t4/check_clock.cpp
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..c698dff
--- /dev/null
+++ b/forge-combo29/tests_t4/check_clock.cpp
@@ -0,0 +1,223 @@
+#include <algorithm>
+#include <chrono>
+#include <cstdlib>
+#include <fstream>
+#include <iostream>
+#include <sstream>
+#include <string>
+#include <utility>
+#include <vector>
+
+namespace {
+
+enum class Kind { Exact, Timed, Short };
+
+struct Expect {
+    Kind kind = Kind::Exact;
+    std::string best;
+    std::string stable;
+    int min_wall_ms = 0;
+    int max_wall_ms = 0;
+    int max_depth = 0;
+    int line = 0;
+};
+
+struct Search {
+    std::string last_info;
+    std::string best;
+    double wall_ms = 0;
+    bool saw_info = false;
+};
+
+std::string trim(std::string text) {
+    while (!text.empty() && (text.back() == '\r' || text.back() == ' ' || text.back() == '\t')) text.pop_back();
+    std::size_t i = 0;
+    while (i < text.size() && (text[i] == ' ' || text[i] == '\t')) ++i;
+    return text.substr(i);
+}
+
+std::vector<Expect> load_expected(const std::string& path) {
+    std::ifstream in(path);
+    if (!in) {
+        std::cerr << "fail: cannot read " << path << "\n";
+        std::exit(2);
+    }
+    std::vector<Expect> out;
+    std::string line;
+    int number = 0;
+    while (std::getline(in, line)) {
+        ++number;
+        line = trim(line);
+        if (line.empty() || line[0] == '#') continue;
+        std::istringstream row(line);
+        std::string kind;
+        if (!(row >> kind)) continue;
+        Expect expect;
+        expect.line = number;
+        if (kind == "exact") {
+            expect.kind = Kind::Exact;
+            if (!(row >> expect.best)) {
+                std::cerr << "fail: expected file line " << number << " has no move\n";
+                std::exit(2);
+            }
+            std::string rest;
+            std::getline(row, rest);
+            expect.stable = trim(rest);
+            if (expect.stable.empty()) {
+                std::cerr << "fail: expected file line " << number << " has no info line\n";
+                std::exit(2);
+            }
+        } else if (kind == "timed") {
+            expect.kind = Kind::Timed;
+            if (!(row >> expect.min_wall_ms >> expect.max_wall_ms)) {
+                std::cerr << "fail: expected file line " << number << " needs min and max wall ms\n";
+                std::exit(2);
+            }
+        } else if (kind == "short") {
+            expect.kind = Kind::Short;
+            if (!(row >> expect.max_wall_ms >> expect.max_depth)) {
+                std::cerr << "fail: expected file line " << number << " needs max wall ms and max depth\n";
+                std::exit(2);
+            }
+        } else {
+            std::cerr << "fail: expected file line " << number << " has unknown kind " << kind << "\n";
+            std::exit(2);
+        }
+        out.push_back(std::move(expect));
+    }
+    return out;
+}
+
+std::string stable_info(const std::string& line) {
+    std::istringstream in(line);
+    std::string token;
+    std::string out;
+    while (in >> token) {
+        if (token == "nps" || token == "hashfull" || token == "time") {
+            std::string skip;
+            in >> skip;
+            continue;
+        }
+        if (!out.empty()) out += ' ';
+        out += token;
+    }
+    return out;
+}
+
+std::string best_move(const std::string& line) {
+    std::istringstream in(line);
+    std::string command;
+    std::string move;
+    in >> command >> move;
+    return move;
+}
+
+int info_depth(const std::string& line) {
+    std::istringstream in(line);
+    std::string info;
+    std::string depth;
+    int value = -1;
+    in >> info >> depth >> value;
+    return value;
+}
+
+std::vector<Search> read_searches() {
+    std::vector<Search> searches;
+    Search current;
+    bool in_search = false;
+    auto started = std::chrono::steady_clock::time_point{};
+    std::string line;
+    while (std::getline(std::cin, line)) {
+        line = trim(line);
+        const auto now = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
+        if (line.rfind("info depth ", 0) == 0) {
+            if (!in_search) {
+                started = now;
+                in_search = true;
+                current = Search{};
+            }
+            current.last_info = line;
+            current.saw_info = true;
+            continue;
+        }
+        if (line.rfind("bestmove ", 0) == 0) {
+            current.best = line;
+            if (in_search) {
+                current.wall_ms = std::chrono::duration<double, std::milli>(now - started).count();
+            }
+            searches.push_back(current);
+            current = Search{};
+            in_search = false;
+        }
+    }
+    return searches;
+}
+
+} // namespace
+
+int main(int argc, char** argv) {
+    if (argc != 2) {
+        std::cerr << "usage: check_clock expected.txt < engine-stdout\n";
+        return 2;
+    }
+    const std::vector<Expect> expected = load_expected(argv[1]);
+    const std::vector<Search> searches = read_searches();
+    int failures = 0;
+    const std::size_t n = std::max(expected.size(), searches.size());
+    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
+        if (i >= expected.size()) {
+            std::cout << "fail " << (i + 1) << ": unexpected extra search\n";
+            ++failures;
+            continue;
+        }
+        if (i >= searches.size()) {
+            std::cout << "fail " << (i + 1) << ": missing search (expected file line " << expected[i].line << ")\n";
+            ++failures;
+            continue;
+        }
+        const Expect& want = expected[i];
+        const Search& got = searches[i];
+        const std::string move = best_move(got.best);
+        const int depth = got.saw_info ? info_depth(got.last_info) : -1;
+        auto fail = [&](const std::string& why) {
+            std::cout << "fail " << (i + 1) << ": " << why << "\n";
+            std::cout << "  wall_ms " << got.wall_ms << " depth " << depth << "\n";
+            std::cout << "  best " << got.best << "\n";
+            if (got.saw_info) std::cout << "  info " << stable_info(got.last_info) << "\n";
+            ++failures;
+        };
+        if (!got.saw_info || move.empty()) {
+            fail("search produced no info depth line or no bestmove");
+            continue;
+        }
+        if (want.kind == Kind::Exact) {
+            const std::string stable = stable_info(got.last_info);
+            if (move != want.best || stable != want.stable) {
+                fail("exact mismatch");
+                std::cout << "  expected best " << want.best << "\n";
+                std::cout << "  expected info " << want.stable << "\n";
+                continue;
+            }
+        } else if (want.kind == Kind::Timed) {
+            if (got.wall_ms < want.min_wall_ms || got.wall_ms > want.max_wall_ms) {
+                fail("wall time outside " + std::to_string(want.min_wall_ms) + ".." +
+                     std::to_string(want.max_wall_ms) + " ms");
+                continue;
+            }
+        } else if (want.kind == Kind::Short) {
+            if (got.wall_ms > want.max_wall_ms || depth > want.max_depth) {
+                fail("expected a short search, wall <= " + std::to_string(want.max_wall_ms) +
+                     " ms and depth <= " + std::to_string(want.max_depth));
+                continue;
+            }
+        }
+        std::cout << "ok " << (i + 1) << " wall_ms " << got.wall_ms << " depth " << depth
+                  << " best " << move << "\n";
+    }
+    if (failures != 0) {
+        std::cout << "fail " << failures << "\n";
+        return 1;
+    }
+    std::cout << "pass\n";
+    return 0;
+}
diff --git a/forge-combo29/tests_t4/clock_commands.txt b/forge-combo29/tests_t4/clock_commands.txt
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..04d1484
--- /dev/null
+++ b/forge-combo29/tests_t4/clock_commands.txt
@@ -0,0 +1,103 @@
+# UCI clock-parser transcript. Threads 1, Hash 16, OwnBook false.
+# Send one line at a time and wait for bestmove after every go. The engine
+# reads the next command on the main thread and that command stops a search
+# still in progress, so a single pipe of this file aborts the searches.
+# Blank lines and lines starting with # are not sent.
+uci
+setoption name Threads value 1
+setoption name Hash value 16
+setoption name OwnBook value false
+setoption name Move Overhead value 0
+isready
+
+# 1. Leading '+' is a positive depth, not a failed parse (depth 1).
+ucinewgame
+position startpos
+go depth +8
+
+# 2. 3000000000 does not fit in a signed 32-bit int. It must not become 0.
+ucinewgame
+position startpos
+go depth 12 wtime 3000000000 btime 3000000000
+
+# 3. First integer above INT_MAX.
+ucinewgame
+position startpos
+go depth 12 wtime 2147483648
+
+# 4. INT_MAX still fits in the old parser and must keep working.
+ucinewgame
+position startpos
+go depth 12 wtime 2147483647
+
+# 5. Bigger than int64: clamp to the clock ceiling, do not become 0.
+ucinewgame
+position startpos
+go depth 12 wtime 999999999999999999999
+
+# 6. An ordinary in-range clock still obeys the depth cap.
+ucinewgame
+position startpos
+go depth 3 wtime 1000
+
+# 7. movetime +80 is 80 ms, not a failed parse.
+ucinewgame
+position startpos
+go movetime +80
+
+# 8. Plain movetime 80, the same budget without a sign.
+ucinewgame
+position startpos
+go movetime 80
+
+# 9. Leading '+' and zeros.
+ucinewgame
+position startpos
+go movetime +00080
+
+# 10. Negative movetime clamps to 0 (a 1 ms budget), not 80 ms.
+ucinewgame
+position startpos
+go movetime -80
+
+# 11. Malformed movetime.
+ucinewgame
+position startpos
+go movetime zz
+
+# 12. Trailing junk is malformed, including after a plus.
+ucinewgame
+position startpos
+go movetime +80ms
+
+# 13. Explicit +0 is zero.
+ucinewgame
+position startpos
+go movetime +0
+
+# 14. Negative wtime clamps to 0, so depth 12 does not finish.
+ucinewgame
+position startpos
+go depth 12 wtime -5
+
+# 15. Black to move: btime 3000000000 is our clock.
+ucinewgame
+position startpos moves e2e4
+go depth 10 btime 3000000000
+
+# 16. Black to move: wtime is the opponent clock and must be ignored.
+ucinewgame
+position startpos moves e2e4
+go depth 10 wtime 3000000000
+
+# 17. White to move: btime 0 is the opponent clock and must be ignored.
+ucinewgame
+position startpos
+go depth 12 btime 0
+
+# 18. winc past INT_MAX counts as increment, so a 200 ms clock is not sudden-death with inc 0.
+ucinewgame
+position startpos
+go wtime 200 winc 3000000000
+
+quit

# Task 3: clock parsing

Base: `lock/combo29-20261110` at `16833ecc03b425586f91f4c8834dea8807bf4c22`.
Branch: `grok47/t3-clock-parse`.

## What was wrong

`parse_limits` in `src/uci.cpp` read `wtime`, `btime`, `winc`, `binc`, and `movetime` with `std::from_chars` into a 32-bit `int`. `3000000000` is larger than `2147483647`, so the conversion failed and the parser returned 0. The search then used a 1 ms limit and answered `bestmove` at once. A leading `+` is also rejected by `std::from_chars`, so `movetime +80` took the same path and became 0.

## The fix

Clock tokens are parsed into a signed 64-bit integer. A single leading `+` is accepted. A leading `-` clamps to 0. A token that is not a complete integer is 0, which is what a bad clock already did. A magnitude that does not fit in 64 bits clamps to `kMaxClockMs` (`INT64_MAX / 256`) instead of becoming 0, so the later multiplications in time allocation stay inside a signed 64-bit integer. `3000000000` is below that ceiling and is kept as written. `depth`, `nodes`, `mate`, and `movestogo` still use the old 32-bit reader.

## Files

- `forge-combo29/include/forge/uci_clock.hpp` (new)
- `forge-combo29/include/forge/search.hpp` (`movetime_ms`, `time_ms`, `increment_ms` are `std::int64_t`)
- `forge-combo29/src/uci.cpp` (clock keywords call `parse_clock_ms`)
- `forge-combo29/tests_t3/clock_parse_test.cpp`
- `forge-combo29/tests_t3/clock_commands.txt`

Engine diff against the lock, not counting the new header: `search.hpp` 8 lines, `uci.cpp` 17 lines. The header is 38 lines.

### UCI clocks

Both binaries were given `Threads 1`, `Hash 16`, `OwnBook false`. Move Overhead stayed at its default of 10. For a clock of `3000000000` the session waited 150 ms and then sent `stop`. Timestamps are seconds after `go`.

Fixed engine, `/tmp/forge-t3/forge`:

`go wtime 3000000000 btime 3000000000` was still searching at 150 ms (last completed info: depth 16, time 137, 267839 nodes). `bestmove e2e4` came back at 0.159 s, after `stop`.

`go movetime +80` returned `bestmove d2d4` at 0.070 s. The last info line was `time 68`.

`go movetime -5` returned `bestmove d2d4` at 0.001 s.

`go movetime abc` returned `bestmove d2d4` at 0.001 s.

`position startpos moves e2e4` then `go wtime 1 btime 3000000000` was still searching at 150 ms (last completed info: depth 17, time 100, 186178 nodes). `bestmove c7c5` came back at 0.162 s, after `stop`.

Lock engine, `/tmp/forge-lock-t3/forge`, same commands, no `stop` required:

`go wtime 3000000000 btime 3000000000` returned `bestmove c2c4` at 0.001 s (depth 5, time 1).

`go movetime +80` returned `bestmove d2d4` at 0.001 s (depth 7, time 1).

`go movetime -5` returned `bestmove d2d4` at 0.001 s.

`go movetime abc` returned `bestmove c2c4` at 0.001 s.

`go wtime 1 btime 3000000000` with Black to move returned `bestmove c7c5` at 0.001 s (depth 7, time 1).

The full info lines from that session are the output of `python3 /tmp/t3_measure.py <engine>` and match the timestamps above. `bench 11`, `bench 13`, and `perft 5` in that same session were 312866, 862329, and 4865609 on both binaries.

## Review follow-up

Codex review on `06d211c9` found two holes in `parse_clock_ms`.

- An overflowing digit run returned the ceiling before checking that the whole token was consumed, so `999999999999999999999abc` became `kMaxClockMs`.
- After a leading `+`, `std::from_chars` still accepted a minus, so `+-80` returned `-80`. `movetime_ms >= 0` is false for that value, and the search then had no clock.

The magnitude is now parsed as an unsigned 64-bit integer, and only after one optional sign. A second sign is rejected. The ceiling is applied only when every character was consumed. Otherwise the token is 0.

```text
g++ -std=c++20 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -I /agent/repos/dwqww/forge-combo29/include /agent/repos/dwqww/forge-combo29/tests_t3/clock_parse_test.cpp -o /tmp/clock_parse_test && /tmp/clock_parse_test
```

```

Both exit codes were 0, and neither compiler printed a diagnostic. On the rebuilt `/tmp/forge-t3/forge`, with `Threads 1`, `Hash 16`, and `OwnBook false`:

- `go movetime +-80`, `go movetime -+80`, `go movetime 999999999999999999999abc`, and `go movetime 9223372036854775808x` each returned `bestmove` at 0.001 s.
- `go movetime +80` returned `bestmove d2d4` at 0.071 s.
- `go wtime 3000000000 btime 3000000000` was still in depth 16 at 0.061 s (`time 60`, 109697 nodes). `bestmove d2d4` came back at 0.162 s, after `stop`.
- `bench 11` = 312866 nodes, `bench 13` = 862329 nodes, `go perft 5` = 4865609 nodes.

## Not verified

- The fixed engine was not left to run for 3000000000 ms. It was stopped at 150 ms while info lines were still arriving.
- AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer were run on `clock_parse_test`, not on the whole `forge` binary.
- `depth`, `nodes`, `mate`, and `movestogo` were not switched to the 64-bit parser. A non-integer or out-of-range value for those keywords still becomes 0, then the old clamp.
- No Elo and no speed claim. The bench node counts match the lock; the recorded bench times were 165 ms and 449 ms on this run.
`````

`````text
+#include "forge/search.hpp"
+
+#include <cstdlib>
+#include <iostream>
+#include <string>
+
+namespace {
+
+constexpr std::string_view Fen =
+    "3r4/Pn1Q1p2/1Q1n1QpN/1p1Q1pRB/1Qbp1QpN/2bQ1pRB/3r1QpK/2k2q2 w - - 0 1";
+
+int losing_captures(const forge::Board& board) {
+    int count = 0;
+    for (const forge::Move move : board.pseudo_legal_moves(true)) {
+        if (!board.see_ge(move, 0)) ++count;
+    }
+    return count;
+}
+
+} // namespace
+
+int main() {
+    forge::Board board;
+    std::string error;
+    if (!board.set_fen(Fen, &error)) {
+        std::cerr << "fen rejected: " << error << "\n";
+        return 1;
+    }
+    const int losing = losing_captures(board);
+    std::cout << "in_check " << (board.in_check() ? 1 : 0) << std::endl;
+    std::cout << "losing_captures " << losing << std::endl;
+    if (board.in_check() || losing <= 64) {
+        std::cerr << "position does not force the 64-slot capture list\n";
+        return 1;
+    }
+
+    forge::Searcher searcher(16, 1);
+    forge::SearchLimits limits;
+    limits.depth = 1;
+    const forge::SearchInfo result = searcher.search(board, limits, false);
+    if (result.best_move.is_none() || !board.is_legal(result.best_move)) {
+        std::cerr << "search did not return a legal move\n";
+        return 1;
+    }
+    std::cout << "bestmove " << forge::Board::move_to_uci(result.best_move) << "\n";
+    std::cout << "nodes " << result.nodes << "\n";
+    return 0;
+}

+bool load_file(std::string_view path, std::string& error) {
+    error.clear();
+    if (path.empty() || path == "<empty>") {
+        live_weights() = make_builtin();
+        return true;
+    }
+    const std::string name(path);
+    std::ifstream input(name, std::ios::binary);
+    if (!input) {
+        error = "nnue: cannot open file";
+        return false;
+    }
+    input.seekg(0, std::ios::end);
+    const std::streamoff length = input.tellg();
+    input.seekg(0);
+    if (length < 0 || static_cast<std::uint64_t>(length) > 2U * 1024U * 1024U) {
+        error = "nnue: wrong size";
+        return false;
+    }
+    std::vector<unsigned char> bytes(static_cast<std::size_t>(length));
+    if (length > 0) input.read(reinterpret_cast<char*>(bytes.data()), length);
+    if (!input || static_cast<std::streamoff>(input.gcount()) != length) {
+        error = "nnue: cannot open file";
+        return false;
+    }
+    if (bytes.size() < 8) {
+        error = "nnue: wrong size";
+        return false;
+    }
+    if (std::memcmp(bytes.data(), "FORGENET", 8) != 0) {
+        error = "nnue: bad magic";
+        return false;
+    }
+    if (bytes.size() < 16) {
+        error = "nnue: wrong size";
+        return false;
+    }
+    if (read_u32(bytes.data() + 8) != 1U) {
+        error = "nnue: unsupported version";
+        return false;
+    }
+    const std::uint32_t hidden = read_u32(bytes.data() + 12);
+    if (hidden != static_cast<std::uint32_t>(HiddenSize) || bytes.size() != kNetBytes) {
+        error = "nnue: wrong size";
+        return false;
+    }
+    std::vector<std::int16_t> w1(static_cast<std::size_t>(InputCount) * HiddenSize);
+    std::vector<std::int16_t> b1(HiddenSize);
+    std::vector<std::int16_t> w2(2 * HiddenSize);
+    const unsigned char* cursor = bytes.data() + 16;
+    auto take = [&cursor](std::vector<std::int16_t>& out) {
+        for (std::int16_t& value : out) {
+            value = read_i16(cursor);
+            cursor += 2;
+        }
+    };
+    take(w1);
+    take(b1);
+    take(w2);
+    const std::int16_t b2 = read_i16(cursor);
+    Weights incoming;
+    quantize(incoming, w1.data(), b1.data(), w2.data(), b2);
+    live_weights() = std::move(incoming);
+    return true;
+}

new file mode 100644
index 0000000..14754cd
--- /dev/null
+++ b/forge-combo29/tests_t8/nnue_convert.cpp
@@ -0,0 +1,59 @@
+#include "forge/nnue.hpp"
+#include "nnue_weights.inc"
+
+#include <cstdint>
+#include <fstream>
+#include <iostream>
+#include <string>
+
+namespace {
+
+void write_u32(std::ostream& out, std::uint32_t value) {
+    const unsigned char bytes[4] = {
+        static_cast<unsigned char>(value),
+        static_cast<unsigned char>(value >> 8),
+        static_cast<unsigned char>(value >> 16),
+        static_cast<unsigned char>(value >> 24),
+    };
+    out.write(reinterpret_cast<const char*>(bytes), 4);
+}
+
+void write_i16(std::ostream& out, std::int16_t value) {
+    const auto bits = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(value);
+    const unsigned char bytes[2] = {
+        static_cast<unsigned char>(bits),
+        static_cast<unsigned char>(bits >> 8),
+    };
+    out.write(reinterpret_cast<const char*>(bytes), 2);
+}
+
+void write_i16s(std::ostream& out, const std::int16_t* data, std::size_t count) {
+    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < count; ++i) write_i16(out, data[i]);
+}
+
+} // namespace
+
+int main(int argc, char** argv) {
+    if (argc != 2) {
+        std::cerr << "usage: nnue_convert <output>\n";
+        return 2;
+    }
+    std::ofstream out(argv[1], std::ios::binary);
+    if (!out) {
+        std::cerr << "cannot write " << argv[1] << '\n';
+        return 1;
+    }
+    out.write("FORGENET", 8);
+    write_u32(out, 1);
+    write_u32(out, static_cast<std::uint32_t>(forge::nnue::HiddenSize));
+    write_i16s(out, NnueW1, sizeof(NnueW1) / sizeof(NnueW1[0]));
+    write_i16s(out, NnueB1, sizeof(NnueB1) / sizeof(NnueB1[0]));
+    write_i16s(out, NnueW2, sizeof(NnueW2) / sizeof(NnueW2[0]));
+    write_i16(out, NnueB2);
+    if (!out) {
+        std::cerr << "write failed\n";
+        return 1;
+    }
+    std::cout << "wrote " << argv[1] << " hidden " << forge::nnue::HiddenSize << '\n';
+    return 0;
+}

+#include "forge/board.hpp"
+#include "forge/nnue.hpp"
+
+#include <cstdint>
+#include <fstream>
+#include <iostream>
+#include <string>
+#include <vector>
+
+namespace {
+
+int failures = 0;
+
+void expect(bool ok, const std::string& name) {
+    if (ok) {
+        std::cout << "ok " << name << '\n';
+        return;
+    }
+    std::cout << "FAIL " << name << '\n';
+    ++failures;
+}
+
+std::vector<unsigned char> read_file(const std::string& path) {
+    std::ifstream input(path, std::ios::binary);
+    input.seekg(0, std::ios::end);
+    const auto length = input.tellg();
+    input.seekg(0);
+    std::vector<unsigned char> bytes(static_cast<std::size_t>(length));
+    if (length > 0) input.read(reinterpret_cast<char*>(bytes.data()), length);
+    return bytes;
+}
+
+void write_file(const std::string& path, const std::vector<unsigned char>& bytes) {
+    std::ofstream output(path, std::ios::binary);
+    output.write(reinterpret_cast<const char*>(bytes.data()), static_cast<std::streamsize>(bytes.size()));
+}
+
+int evaluate_fen(const char* fen) {
+    forge::Board board;
+    if (!board.set_fen(fen)) return 999999;
+    forge::nnue::Accumulator accumulator;
+    forge::nnue::refresh(board, accumulator);
+    return forge::nnue::evaluate(board, accumulator);
+}
+
+} // namespace
+
+int main(int argc, char** argv) {
+    if (argc != 2) {
+        std::cerr << "usage: nnue_file_test <lock-net>\n";
+        return 2;
+    }
+    const std::string net_path = argv[1];
+    const char* start = "rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/8/8/PPPPPPPP/RNBQKBNR w KQkq - 0 1";
+    const char* kiwipete = "r3k2r/p1ppqpb1/bn2pnp1/3PN3/1p2P3/2N2Q1p/PPPBBPPP/R3K2R w KQkq - 0 1";
+    const int start_builtin = evaluate_fen(start);
+    const int kiwi_builtin = evaluate_fen(kiwipete);
+
+    std::string error;
+    const bool loaded = forge::nnue::load_file(net_path, error);
+    expect(loaded && error.empty(), "load converted net");
+    expect(evaluate_fen(start) == start_builtin, "startpos eval matches built-in net");
+    expect(evaluate_fen(kiwipete) == kiwi_builtin, "kiwipete eval matches built-in net");
+
+    std::vector<unsigned char> bytes = read_file(net_path);
+    expect(bytes.size() > 16 && bytes.size() >= 8, "converted file is non-empty");
+
+    auto shifted = bytes;
+    const std::uint16_t bias = std::uint16_t(shifted[shifted.size() - 2]) |
+                               (std::uint16_t(shifted[shifted.size() - 1]) << 8);
+    const std::uint16_t bumped = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(bias + 2000);
+    shifted[shifted.size() - 2] = static_cast<unsigned char>(bumped);
+    shifted[shifted.size() - 1] = static_cast<unsigned char>(bumped >> 8);
+    const std::string shifted_path = net_path + ".shifted";
+    write_file(shifted_path, shifted);
+    expect(forge::nnue::load_file(shifted_path, error), "load shifted bias");
+    const bool changed = evaluate_fen(start) != start_builtin || evaluate_fen(kiwipete) != kiwi_builtin;
+    expect(changed, "shifted bias changes an evaluation");
+
+    expect(forge::nnue::load_file("", error) && error.empty(), "empty path restores built-in net");
+    expect(evaluate_fen(start) == start_builtin && evaluate_fen(kiwipete) == kiwi_builtin,
+           "restored eval matches built-in net");
+
+    auto magic = bytes;
+    magic[0] = 'X';
+    write_file(net_path + ".magic", magic);
+    expect(!forge::nnue::load_file(net_path + ".magic", error) && error == "nnue: bad magic",
+           "bad magic keeps the current net");
+    expect(evaluate_fen(start) == start_builtin, "eval unchanged after bad magic");
+
+    auto version = bytes;
+    version[8] = 2;
+    write_file(net_path + ".version", version);
+    expect(!forge::nnue::load_file(net_path + ".version", error) && error == "nnue: unsupported version",
+           "wrong version keeps the current net");
+
+    auto hidden = bytes;
+    hidden[12] = 128;
+    hidden[13] = 0;
+    write_file(net_path + ".hidden", hidden);
+    expect(!forge::nnue::load_file(net_path + ".hidden", error) && error == "nnue: wrong size",
+           "wrong hidden size keeps the current net");
+
+    auto truncated = bytes;
+    truncated.pop_back();
+    write_file(net_path + ".short", truncated);
+    expect(!forge::nnue::load_file(net_path + ".short", error) && error == "nnue: wrong size",
+           "truncated file keeps the current net");
+
+    auto extra = bytes;
+    extra.push_back(0);
+    write_file(net_path + ".extra", extra);
+    expect(!forge::nnue::load_file(net_path + ".extra", error) && error == "nnue: wrong size",
+           "oversized file keeps the current net");
+
+    expect(!forge::nnue::load_file(net_path + ".missing", error) && error == "nnue: cannot open file",
+           "missing file keeps the current net");
+    expect(evaluate_fen(start) == start_builtin && evaluate_fen(kiwipete) == kiwi_builtin,
+           "eval unchanged after rejected files");
+
+    if (failures != 0) {
+        std::cout << failures << " failed\n";
+        return 1;
+    }
+    std::cout << "PASS\n";
+    return 0;
+}
+ git show 48644054dd67fd5abf547cd00de1c9943411baf9:forge-combo29/REPORT_t1.md
# Task 1: capture list overflow

## What was wrong

`MovePicker` keeps SEE-losing captures in `bad_captures_`, a `std::array<Move, 64>`, and stores them with `bad_captures_[bad_count_++] = move` (`src/search.cpp`, the write at line 469 on the lock). Nothing stops `bad_count_` at 64. The move generator can emit more than 64 captures in a legal position, and the main-search picker stores every capture that fails `see_ge(move, 0)`.

The position `3r4/Pn1Q1p2/1Q1n1QpN/1p1Q1pRB/1Qbp1QpN/2bQ1pRB/3r1QpK/2k2q2 w - - 0 1` is legal, not in check, and has 68 pseudo-legal captures with negative SEE. A depth-1 search of that position writes past the array.

## The fix

`bad_captures_` is now `std::array<Move, MoveList::Capacity>`. `MoveList::Capacity` is 256, the same bound as the generator that fills the picker. Both the uninitialized and the zero-initialized declarations were changed, so a build that does not define `FORGE_SPD_NO_ZERO_MOVELISTS` is covered too. The picker still stores every losing capture and still returns them in the same order. Positions that never pass 64 losing captures, including the bench set, walk the same prefix of the array.

## Files changed

- `forge-combo29/src/search.cpp`
- `forge-combo29/tests_t1/bad_capture_overflow.cpp`
- `forge-combo29/REPORT_t1.md`

Engine source diff: 4 insertions, 2 deletions.

## Commands and output

`/usr/bin/c++` on this machine is Clang 18.1.3 and cannot link a CMake probe (`cannot find -lstdc++`). The release build below uses `/usr/bin/g++` (GCC 13.3.0). The machine has AVX-512, so `FORGE_PORTABLE` was left off.

```

The build completed and produced `/tmp/forge-t1/release/forge`.

## Not verified

- The release binary was not itself rebuilt with ASan. The sanitizer run is the test program.
- No Elo and no speed comparison. The `nps` lines above are the timing of this one release run.
- `FORGE_SDK_BADCAP_PREFIX` stays 0. That switch stores losing captures in the consumed front of `moves_` instead of `bad_captures_`. It was not enabled and not benched.
- A position that generated more than 256 captures was not run. The generator stores at most `MoveList::Capacity` moves, and with `NDEBUG` its `assert` is compiled out. This change makes the capture list as large as that generator buffer. It does not add a new check inside `MoveList::push_back`.
+ git show 3757595a97ede6978f39e826e33b85354c458ed3:forge-combo29/REPORT_t8.md
# Task 8: load an NNUE net from a file

The lock engine can evaluate only the network compiled in from `src/nnue_weights.inc`. There is no way to point it at another net of the same shape.

`NnueFile` is a string UCI option, default `<empty>`. An empty value or `<empty>` installs the compiled-in net. Any other value is read as a `FORGENET` file: 8-byte magic, little-endian uint32 version 1, little-endian uint32 hidden size, then little-endian int16 `W1`, `B1`, `W2`, and one int16 `B2`. The hidden size must equal the compiled `HiddenSize` (256) and the file must be exactly 394770 bytes. A wrong magic, version, or size prints `info string` with the reason and leaves the current net in place. A successful load replaces the live weights, clears the hash, and prints `info string loaded nnue <path>`. With the option left unset, the weight conversion is the same division by 4096 as before, so bench and perft stay on the lock counts.

## What was not verified

- The engine binary itself was not rebuilt with AddressSanitizer or UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer. The sanitizer run is the test program above.
- No net with a hidden size other than 256 was installed. A file that declares hidden size 128 is rejected as `nnue: wrong size`.
- The reader was not run on a big-endian machine. The integers are decoded from little-endian bytes on this x86-64 host.
- No strength or speed comparison was made. The `nps` figures above are the engine's own printout for those runs.

#include "forge/nnue.hpp"

#include <algorithm>
#include <cmath>
#include <cstdint>
#include <memory>

// The output layer uses SSE min/max/mul/add directly: compilers may not turn a
// float clamp into min/max instructions without -ffast-math, which left the
// AVX2 builds with slow scalar code. SSE2 is part of every x86-64 target.
#if defined(__SSE__) || defined(_M_X64) || defined(_M_AMD64)
#include <xmmintrin.h>
#define FORGE_NNUE_SSE 1
#else
#define FORGE_NNUE_SSE 0
#endif

#if defined(__AVX2__)
#include <immintrin.h>
#endif

#if !defined(__AVX512F__)
#error "FORGE_SPD_NNUE_ZMM=1 needs an AVX-512F target (the lock builds with -march=znver5)"
#endif
#include <immintrin.h>
#endif

#if __has_include("nnue_weights.inc")
#include "nnue_weights.inc"
#define FORGE_HAS_NNUE 1
#else
#define FORGE_HAS_NNUE 0
#endif
// Include files written before residual training existed carry no flag and
// hold stand-alone networks.
#ifndef FORGE_NNUE_RESIDUAL
#define FORGE_NNUE_RESIDUAL 0
#endif
#if FORGE_HAS_NNUE
static_assert(sizeof(NnueW1) / sizeof(NnueW1[0]) == static_cast<std::size_t>(forge::nnue::InputCount) * forge::nnue::HiddenSize,
              "nnue_weights.inc was trained for a different FORGE_NNUE_HIDDEN");
static_assert(sizeof(NnueB1) / sizeof(NnueB1[0]) == static_cast<std::size_t>(forge::nnue::HiddenSize), "nnue_weights.inc b1 size");

#endif

namespace forge::nnue {

bool enabled = true;

namespace {

struct Weights {
    std::unique_ptr<float[]> w1;   // [InputCount][HiddenSize]
    alignas(32) std::array<float, HiddenSize> b1{};
#if FORGE_SPD_NNUE_ZMM
    alignas(64) std::array<float, 2 * HiddenSize> w2{};
#else
    alignas(32) std::array<float, 2 * HiddenSize> w2{};
#endif
    float b2 = 0.0F;
};

const Weights& weights() {
    static const Weights instance = [] {
        Weights w;
        w.w1 = std::make_unique<float[]>(static_cast<std::size_t>(InputCount) * HiddenSize);
#if FORGE_HAS_NNUE
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < static_cast<std::size_t>(InputCount) * HiddenSize; ++i) {
            w.w1[i] = static_cast<float>(NnueW1[i]) / WeightScale;
        }
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < HiddenSize; ++i) w.b1[i] = static_cast<float>(NnueB1[i]) / WeightScale;
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < 2 * HiddenSize; ++i) w.w2[i] = static_cast<float>(NnueW2[i]) / OutputScale;
        w.b2 = static_cast<float>(NnueB2) / OutputScale;
#endif
        return w;
    }();
    return instance;
}

inline void add_feature(std::array<float, HiddenSize>& acc, const float* column) {
    for (int h = 0; h < HiddenSize; ++h) acc[static_cast<std::size_t>(h)] += column[h];
}

inline void sub_feature(std::array<float, HiddenSize>& acc, const float* column) {
    for (int h = 0; h < HiddenSize; ++h) acc[static_cast<std::size_t>(h)] -= column[h];
}

} // namespace

bool available() { return FORGE_HAS_NNUE != 0; }

bool residual() { return FORGE_HAS_NNUE != 0 && FORGE_NNUE_RESIDUAL != 0; }

void refresh(const Board& board, Accumulator& accumulator) {
    const Weights& w = weights();
    for (const Color perspective : {White, Black}) {
        auto& acc = accumulator.values[static_cast<std::size_t>(perspective)];
        acc = w.b1;
        Bitboard occupied = board.occupied();
        while (occupied != 0) {
            const int square = pop_lsb(occupied);
            const int index = feature_index(perspective, board.piece_at(square), square);
            add_feature(acc, w.w1.get() + static_cast<std::size_t>(index) * HiddenSize);
        }
    }
    accumulator.valid = true;
}
`````

`````text
diff --git a/forge-combo29/tests_t5/krk_mate_test.cpp b/forge-combo29/tests_t5/krk_mate_test.cpp
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..695b056
--- /dev/null
+++ b/forge-combo29/tests_t5/krk_mate_test.cpp
@@ -0,0 +1,132 @@
+// KRK mate stability. On the unchanged lock this program fails two ways:
+// a Threads 1 search keeps move-ordering history from an earlier position and
+// then plays a different move (often without a mate score), and Threads 2
+// stores helper transposition bounds that make the same depth-14 search
+// disagree with Threads 1.
+#include "forge/search.hpp"
+
+#include <iostream>
+#include <string>
+#include <utility>
+
+namespace {
+
+struct Result {
+    std::string move;
+    int score = 0;
+    bool ok = false;
+};
+
+std::string score_text(int score) {
+    if (forge::is_mate_score(score)) {
+        const int distance = forge::MateValue - std::abs(score);
+        const int mate = (distance + 1) / 2;
+        return "mate " + std::to_string(score > 0 ? mate : -mate);
+    }
+    return "cp " + std::to_string(score);
+}
+
+Result search_fen(forge::Searcher& searcher, const std::string& fen, int depth) {
+    Result result;
+    forge::Board board;
+    std::string error;
+    if (!board.set_fen(fen, &error)) {
+        std::cout << "invalid fen: " << error << "\n";
+        return result;
+    }
+    forge::SearchLimits limits;
+    limits.depth = depth;
+    const forge::SearchInfo info = searcher.search(board, limits, false, forge::Searcher::TTAccess::Exclusive);
+    result.move = forge::Board::move_to_uci(info.best_move);
+    result.score = info.score;
+    result.ok = true;
+    return result;
+}
+
+bool same(const Result& a, const Result& b) {
+    return a.ok && b.ok && a.move == b.move && a.score == b.score;
+}
+
+void print_result(const char* label, const std::string& fen, const Result& result) {
+    std::cout << label << " " << fen << " " << score_text(result.score) << " " << result.move << "\n";
+}
+
+int check_history(const std::string& fen) {
+    constexpr const char* kStart = "rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/8/8/PPPPPPPP/RNBQKBNR w KQkq - 0 1";
+    forge::Searcher clean(16, 1);
+    const Result expected = search_fen(clean, fen, 14);
+    print_result("fresh", fen, expected);
+    if (!expected.ok || !forge::is_mate_score(expected.score)) {
+        std::cout << "history FAIL: fresh search did not prove a mate\n";
+        return 1;
+    }
+    forge::Searcher stained(16, 1);
+    const Result prelude = search_fen(stained, kStart, 10);
+    if (!prelude.ok) return 1;
+    // Drop the previous table only. History tables stay, which is the bug.
+    stained.clear_hash();
+    const Result after = search_fen(stained, fen, 14);
+    print_result("after-startpos", fen, after);
+    if (!same(expected, after)) {
+        std::cout << "history FAIL\n";
+        return 1;
+    }
+    std::cout << "history ok\n";
+    return 0;
+}
+
+int check_threads(const std::string& fen, bool use_nnue, int runs) {
+    forge::nnue::enabled = use_nnue;
+    forge::Searcher one(16, 1);
+    const Result expected = search_fen(one, fen, 14);
+    print_result(use_nnue ? "nnue-t1" : "t1", fen, expected);
+    if (!expected.ok) return 1;
+    if (!use_nnue && !forge::is_mate_score(expected.score)) {
+        std::cout << "threads FAIL: Threads 1 did not prove a mate\n";
+        return 1;
+    }
+    forge::Searcher two(16, 2);
+    int mismatches = 0;
+    Result first_mismatch{};
+    for (int i = 0; i < runs; ++i) {
+        two.clear();
+        const Result got = search_fen(two, fen, 14);
+        if (!same(expected, got)) {
+            if (mismatches == 0) first_mismatch = got;
+            ++mismatches;
+        }
+    }
+    std::cout << (use_nnue ? "nnue-threads2 " : "threads2 ") << fen << " runs " << runs
+              << " mismatches " << mismatches;
+    if (mismatches > 0) {
+        std::cout << " first " << score_text(first_mismatch.score) << " " << first_mismatch.move;
+    }
+    std::cout << "\n";
+    if (mismatches > 0) {
+        std::cout << "threads FAIL\n";
+        return 1;
+    }
+    std::cout << "threads ok\n";
+    return 0;
+}
+
+} // namespace
+
+int main() {
+    forge::nnue::enabled = false;
+    const char* positions[] = {
+        "4K3/k7/8/8/2R5/8/8/8 w - - 0 1",
+        "8/8/8/8/8/1R6/2k5/5K2 w - - 0 1",
+        "3k4/8/3K4/8/8/8/8/3R4 w - - 0 1",
+    };
+    int failures = 0;
+    for (const char* fen : positions) failures += check_history(fen);
+    for (const char* fen : positions) failures += check_threads(fen, false, 30);
+    failures += check_threads("4K3/k7/8/8/2R5/8/8/8 w - - 0 1", true, 20);
+    if (failures != 0) {
+        std::cout << "FAILED " << failures << "\n";
+        return 1;
+    }
+    std::cout << "ok\n";
+    return 0;
+}

diff --git a/forge-combo29/tests_t6/fixed_nodes.cpp b/forge-combo29/tests_t6/fixed_nodes.cpp
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..8b55332
--- /dev/null
+++ b/forge-combo29/tests_t6/fixed_nodes.cpp
@@ -0,0 +1,108 @@
+#include "forge/board.hpp"
+#include "forge/search.hpp"
+
+#include <cstdlib>
+#include <iostream>
+#include <string>
+#include <string_view>
+
+// `go nodes` used to keep the previous iteration's score and take a best move
+// from the iteration the limit cut off. The score and the move must be the
+// pair produced by the last iteration that actually finished.
+
+namespace {
+
+int g_failures = 0;
+
+struct Outcome {
+    int score = 0;
+    int depth = 0;
+    std::uint64_t nodes = 0;
+    std::string move;
+};
+
+Outcome search_fen(std::string_view fen, int depth, std::uint64_t nodes, bool use_nodes) {
+    forge::Board board;
+    if (!board.set_fen(fen)) {
+        std::cerr << "bad fen " << fen << std::endl;
+        std::exit(2);
+    }
+    forge::Searcher searcher(16, 1);
+    forge::SearchLimits limits;
+    if (use_nodes) {
+        limits.nodes = nodes;
+        limits.nodes_specified = true;
+        limits.depth = 32;
+    } else {
+        limits.depth = depth;
+    }
+    const forge::SearchInfo info =
+        searcher.search(board, limits, false, forge::Searcher::TTAccess::Exclusive);
+    Outcome out;
+    out.score = info.score;
+    out.depth = info.depth;
+    out.nodes = info.nodes;
+    out.move = info.best_move.is_none() ? "none" : forge::Board::move_to_uci(info.best_move);
+    return out;
+}
+
+void check_span(std::string_view fen) {
+    std::cout << "fen " << fen << std::endl;
+    Outcome previous = search_fen(fen, 1, 0, false);
+    std::cout << "depth 1 score " << previous.score << " move " << previous.move
+              << " nodes " << previous.nodes << std::endl;
+    bool saw_change = false;
+    for (int depth = 2; depth <= 8 && !saw_change; ++depth) {
+        const Outcome current = search_fen(fen, depth, 0, false);
+        std::cout << "depth " << depth << " score " << current.score << " move " << current.move
+                  << " nodes " << current.nodes << std::endl;
+        if (current.move == previous.move) {
+            previous = current;
+            continue;
+        }
+        saw_change = true;
+        std::cout << "span depth " << previous.depth << " nodes " << previous.nodes << " -> depth "
+                  << current.depth << " nodes " << current.nodes << std::endl;
+        if (current.nodes <= previous.nodes + 1) {
+            std::cout << "FAIL span too small" << std::endl;
+            ++g_failures;
+            return;
+        }
+        const std::uint64_t step = std::max<std::uint64_t>(1, (current.nodes - previous.nodes) / 8);
+        for (std::uint64_t budget = previous.nodes + 1; budget < current.nodes; budget += step) {
+            const Outcome limited = search_fen(fen, 0, budget, true);
+            if (limited.depth <= 0) {
+                std::cout << "nodes " << budget << " depth 0 score " << limited.score << " move "
+                          << limited.move << std::endl;
+                if (limited.score != 0) {
+                    std::cout << "FAIL unfinished search published a score" << std::endl;
+                    ++g_failures;
+                }
+                continue;
+            }
+            const Outcome finished = search_fen(fen, limited.depth, 0, false);
+            const bool match = limited.score == finished.score && limited.move == finished.move;
+            std::cout << "nodes " << budget << " depth " << limited.depth << " score " << limited.score
+                      << " move " << limited.move << " finished-score " << finished.score
+                      << " finished-move " << finished.move << (match ? " PASS" : " FAIL") << std::endl;
+            if (!match) ++g_failures;
+        }
+    }
+    if (!saw_change) {
+        std::cout << "FAIL no depth changed the best move" << std::endl;
+        ++g_failures;
+    }
+}
+
+} // namespace
+
+int main() {
+    check_span("rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/8/8/PPPPPPPP/RNBQKBNR w KQkq - 0 1");
+    check_span("8/8/8/8/4k3/8/3R4/4K3 w - - 0 1");
+    if (g_failures != 0) {
+        std::cout << "FAIL failures " << g_failures << std::endl;
+        return 1;
+    }
+    std::cout << "PASS fixed-node score and move agree" << std::endl;
+    return 0;
+}
+ git show 1c3a5e0a11043c0d91d683f40691dd386a5158e4:forge-combo29/REPORT_t5.md
# Task 5: two-thread KRK mate, and stale history

## What was wrong

With `Threads 2`, a depth-14 search of a king-and-rook ending does not stay on the mate that `Threads 1` proves. Helper threads write the shared transposition table. A PV node may skip legal moves (late-move pruning, history pruning, futility, SEE) and still store `BoundExact` or `BoundUpper`. `BoundExact` replaces the existing entry at any depth, so a helper store overwrites the main thread's mate score. The main thread then cuts off and reports a different move, sometimes a centipawn score. Helper probes also rewrite an entry's generation, which changes which slot the main thread replaces.

With `Threads 1`, the history tables live until `ucinewgame`. They are indexed by from-square and to-square, not by position. After another search, and after `Clear Hash` has wiped the table, the same ending can play a different move and lose the mate score. `ucinewgame` hides this because it clears the histories.

## Fix

Helper threads still read the table and still search, but they no longer store entries and they no longer refresh generation on a probe. The main thread's stores are unchanged, so a one-thread search builds the same table as before. Every search, on every worker, clears that worker's history tables before the root. Bench already clears those tables before each position, and the depth-11 and depth-13 node counts stayed on the lock pins.

## Files

- `forge-combo29/include/forge/search.hpp`
- `forge-combo29/src/search.cpp`
- `forge-combo29/tests_t5/krk_mate_test.cpp`
- `forge-combo29/REPORT_t5.md`

Engine diff: 38 insertions, 16 deletions (`git diff --numstat`). No change to `CMakeLists.txt`.

The test links `Searcher` directly (`TTAccess::Exclusive`, Hash 16). It fails on the lock sources and passes after the change. `UseNNUE` is off for the mate checks. One extra block leaves the net on and only checks that two threads repeat the one-thread move and score.

## Commands

Working directory: `/agent/repos/dwqww`. Compiler: `g++-13` (this machine's Clang 18 does not link). CPU supports the lock `-march=x86-64-v4` build. The test binary is not part of the branch.
`````
