`````text
# Task 6: fixed-node score and move

Branch `grok47/t6-fixed-node-score`, from `lock/combo29-20261110` at `16833ecc03b425586f91f4c8834dea8807bf4c22`. Compiler: `g++ (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0`.

## What was wrong

`go nodes N` can finish one or more iterations and then stop in the middle of the next one. If a root move in that unfinished iteration raises alpha, the old code keeps that move and its PV, but it does not update the score. The score stays the one from the last finished iteration.

On the start position, the same session against `/tmp/forge-t6-lock/forge` (built from `16833ecc` before this change) printed:

```
info depth 3 seldepth 3 score cp 49 nodes 155 nps 0 hashfull 0 time 0 pv c2c4 h7h6 d2d4
bestmove c2c4
```

Depth 2 had already finished as `d2d4` with score 49. Depth 3's finished result is `e2e4` with score 18, at 215 nodes. The 155-node search published `c2c4` together with the depth-2 score 49.

## The fix

`Worker::should_stop` records when the node budget is the reason it returns. If that flag is set, the abort path leaves the best move, PV, and score on the last iteration that finished, and it does not print a new `info` line. A clock stop or an external `stop` still keeps a partial root move, which is the previous behaviour. Engine diff: 14 insertions and 4 deletions in `src/search.cpp` and `include/forge/search.hpp`.

## Files

- `forge-combo29/src/search.cpp`
- `forge-combo29/include/forge/search.hpp`
- `forge-combo29/tests_t6/fixed_nodes.cpp`
- `forge-combo29/REPORT_t6.md`

- A movetime or `wtime` game in which a partial root move used to replace the finished move. That path is still the old `if` body; only a node-budget stop skips it. Wall-clock stops are not repeatable on this machine, so they were not compared byte for byte.
- `go nodes` with more than one thread.
- A node budget that expires before depth 1 finishes. The reported score stays 0 and the move stays the first legal root move.
- The lock's Windows ThinLTO/PGO build, and `-DFORGE_PORTABLE=ON`.
- No Elo or speed claim. `time` and `nps` in the bench lines above are this run only.

std::uint64_t Worker::total_nodes() const {
    std::uint64_t total = local_nodes_;
    if (all_workers_ != nullptr) {
        for (const Worker* worker : *all_workers_) {
            if (worker != this) total += worker->nodes();
        }
    }
    return total;
}

bool Worker::should_stop() {
    // Publish this thread's node count for the others at the same cadence.
    nodes_.store(local_nodes_, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    if (shared_.stop.load(std::memory_order_relaxed)) return true;
    if (!is_main()) return false;
    if (node_limit_specified_ && total_nodes() >= node_limit_) return true;
    if (hard_limit_ms_ > 0) {
        if (pondering_ && shared_.ponder_hit_ns.load(std::memory_order_relaxed) == 0) return false;
        if (elapsed_ms() >= hard_limit_ms_) return true;
    }
    return false;
}

bool Worker::is_draw(const Board& board, int ply) const {
    (void)ply;
    if (board.halfmove_clock() >= 100) {
        // Checkmate on the hundredth half-move still wins; everything else is a draw.
        return !board.in_check() || board.has_legal_move();
    }
    // Detect stalemate before TT cutoffs, stand pat or forward pruning can
    if (nnue::enabled && nnue::available()) {
        nnue::refresh(board, ss->accumulator);
        if (nnue::residual()) ss->runtime_psqt = Evaluator::refresh_runtime_psqt(board);
    }

    Move previous_best = Move::none();
    int stable_iterations = 0;
    int score = 0;
    int previous_score = ValueNone;
    root_effort_count_ = root_candidates.size();
    assert(root_effort_count_ <= root_effort_moves_.size());
    std::copy(root_candidates.begin(), root_candidates.end(), root_effort_moves_.begin());
    root_move_nodes_.fill(0);
    for (int depth = 1; depth <= max_depth; ++depth) {
        root_depth_ = depth;
        int delta = tune::AspirationDelta;
        int alpha = -Infinite;
        int beta = Infinite;
        if (depth >= 4) {
            alpha = std::max(score - delta, -Infinite);
            beta = std::min(score + delta, Infinite);
        }
        int iteration_score = score;
        while (true) {
            ss->ply = 0;
            iteration_score = search(board, ss, depth, alpha, beta, false);
            if (aborted_) break;
            if (iteration_score <= alpha) {
                beta = (alpha + beta) / 2;
                alpha = std::max(iteration_score - delta, -Infinite);
            } else if (iteration_score >= beta) {
                beta = std::min(iteration_score + delta, Infinite);
            } else {
                break;
            }
            delta += delta / 2 + 4;
        }
        if (aborted_) {
            // A partially searched iteration that already raised alpha at the
            // root has found a move at least as good as the previous best.
            if (ss->pv_length > 0 && !(result.pv.size() > 0 && result.pv[0] == ss->pv[0])) {
                result.best_move = ss->pv[0];
                result.pv.assign(ss->pv.begin(), ss->pv.begin() + ss->pv_length);
                result.ponder_move = result.pv.size() > 1 ? result.pv[1] : Move::none();
                // Publish the revised line so GUIs see a PV consistent with the move.
                emit(depth, result.score, result.pv);
            }
            break;
        }
        score = iteration_score;
        result.score = score;
        result.depth = depth;
        result.seldepth = std::max(seldepth_, depth);
        result.pv.assign(ss->pv.begin(), ss->pv.begin() + ss->pv_length);
        if (!result.pv.empty()) result.best_move = result.pv.front();
        result.ponder_move = result.pv.size() > 1 ? result.pv[1] : Move::none();
        result.nodes = total_nodes();
        emit(depth, score, result.pv);

        if (result.best_move == previous_best) ++stable_iterations;
        else stable_iterations = 0;
        previous_best = result.best_move;
        const int iteration_previous_score = previous_score;
        previous_score = score;

        if (mate_moves > 0 && is_mate_score(score) && MateValue - std::abs(score) <= mate_depth) break;
        if (should_stop()) break;
        if (time_managed_ && !(pondering_ && shared_.ponder_hit_ns.load(std::memory_order_relaxed) == 0)) {
            // Stop early when the best move has been stable; spend longer when it keeps changing.
            double factor = 1.0;
            if (stable_iterations >= 6) factor = tune::TmStableFactor / 100.0;
            else if (stable_iterations >= 3) factor = tune::TmSemiStableFactor / 100.0;
            else if (stable_iterations == 0 && depth >= 6) factor = tune::TmUnstableFactor / 100.0;
            // A best move that absorbed most of the effort is clearly best;
            // spend longer when the alternatives still draw attention.
            if (local_nodes_ > 0 && depth >= 6) {
                const auto effort_end = root_effort_moves_.begin() + static_cast<std::ptrdiff_t>(root_effort_count_);
                const auto best_effort = std::find(root_effort_moves_.begin(), effort_end, result.best_move);
                if (best_effort != effort_end) {
                    const auto index = static_cast<std::size_t>(best_effort - root_effort_moves_.begin());
                    const double effort = static_cast<double>(root_move_nodes_[index]) / static_cast<double>(local_nodes_);
                    factor *= std::clamp(tune::TmEffortBase / 100.0 - effort, 0.6, 1.4);
                }
            }
            // A falling evaluation deserves more thought.
            if (iteration_previous_score != ValueNone && !is_mate_score(score) && score < iteration_previous_score) {
                const int drop = std::min(iteration_previous_score - score, 150);
                factor *= 1.0 + drop * tune::TmFallingEvalPercent / 10000.0;
            }
            factor = std::max(factor, tune::TmMinFactorPercent / 100.0);
            if (elapsed_ms() >= static_cast<std::int64_t>(static_cast<double>(soft_limit_ms_) * factor)) break;
        }
    }

    nodes_.store(local_nodes_, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    result.nodes = total_nodes();
    result.seldepth = std::max(result.seldepth, seldepth_);
    result.elapsed_ms = static_cast<std::uint64_t>(std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(
        std::chrono::steady_clock::now() - start_).count());
    if (result.best_move.is_none()) result.best_move = root_candidates.front();
    return result;
}

}

SearchInfo Searcher::search(Board board, const SearchLimits& limits, bool emit_info, TTAccess table_access) {
    const auto supplied_start = limits.start_time != std::chrono::steady_clock::time_point{}
        ? limits.start_time : limits.request_start;
    const bool clocked = !limits.infinite && !limits.ponder &&
        (limits.time_ms >= 0 || limits.movetime_ms >= 0);
    const auto origin = supplied_start == std::chrono::steady_clock::time_point{} && clocked
        ? std::chrono::steady_clock::now() : supplied_start;
    SearchLimits worker_limits = limits;
    worker_limits.start_time = origin;
    std::vector<Worker*> all;
    all.reserve(workers_.size());
    for (auto& worker : workers_) all.push_back(worker.get());
    // Age the table once per search, before any worker can probe it.
    shared_.tt.new_search();
    std::optional<TranspositionTable::ExclusiveLease> exclusive;
    if (table_access == TTAccess::Exclusive && workers_.size() == 1) {
        exclusive.emplace(shared_.tt);
    }
#if FORGE_SPD_TT_NOTLS
    // This thread holds the lease (if one was taken) and runs the main worker
    // below; helpers exist only without a lease. Saved and restored, so a throw
    // or a nested search leaves the flag as it was.
    struct TtOwnedScope {
        Worker& worker;
        const bool previous;
        TtOwnedScope(Worker& w, bool owned) : worker(w), previous(w.tt_owned_) { worker.tt_owned_ = owned; }
        ~TtOwnedScope() { worker.tt_owned_ = previous; }
        TtOwnedScope(const TtOwnedScope&) = delete;
        TtOwnedScope& operator=(const TtOwnedScope&) = delete;
    } tt_owned_scope(*workers_.front(), exclusive.has_value());
#endif
    std::vector<std::thread> helpers;
    for (std::size_t i = 1; i < workers_.size(); ++i) {
        helpers.emplace_back([this, i, board, &worker_limits, &all]() {
            (void)workers_[i]->search(board, worker_limits, false, all);
        });
    }
    SearchInfo result = workers_.front()->search(board, worker_limits, emit_info, all);
    // Wind down the helpers without clobbering an externally requested stop.
    const bool external_stop = shared_.stop.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
    shared_.stop.store(true, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    for (auto& helper : helpers) helper.join();
    shared_.stop.store(external_stop, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    return result;
}

} // namespace forge
`````

`````text
diff --git a/forge-combo29/tests_t5/krk_mate_test.cpp b/forge-combo29/tests_t5/krk_mate_test.cpp

index 0000000..695b056
--- /dev/null
+++ b/forge-combo29/tests_t5/krk_mate_test.cpp
@@ -0,0 +1,132 @@
+// KRK mate stability. On the unchanged lock this program fails two ways:
+// a Threads 1 search keeps move-ordering history from an earlier position and
+// then plays a different move (often without a mate score), and Threads 2
+// stores helper transposition bounds that make the same depth-14 search
+// disagree with Threads 1.
+#include "forge/search.hpp"
+
+#include <iostream>
+#include <string>
+#include <utility>
+
+namespace {
+
+struct Result {
+    std::string move;
+    int score = 0;
+    bool ok = false;
+};
+
+std::string score_text(int score) {
+    if (forge::is_mate_score(score)) {
+        const int distance = forge::MateValue - std::abs(score);
+        const int mate = (distance + 1) / 2;
+        return "mate " + std::to_string(score > 0 ? mate : -mate);
+    }
+    return "cp " + std::to_string(score);
+}
+
+Result search_fen(forge::Searcher& searcher, const std::string& fen, int depth) {
+    Result result;
+    forge::Board board;
+    std::string error;
+    if (!board.set_fen(fen, &error)) {
+        std::cout << "invalid fen: " << error << "\n";
+        return result;
+    }
+    forge::SearchLimits limits;
+    limits.depth = depth;
+    const forge::SearchInfo info = searcher.search(board, limits, false, forge::Searcher::TTAccess::Exclusive);
+    result.move = forge::Board::move_to_uci(info.best_move);
+    result.score = info.score;
+    result.ok = true;
+    return result;
+}
+
+bool same(const Result& a, const Result& b) {
+    return a.ok && b.ok && a.move == b.move && a.score == b.score;
+}
+
+void print_result(const char* label, const std::string& fen, const Result& result) {
+    std::cout << label << " " << fen << " " << score_text(result.score) << " " << result.move << "\n";
+}
+
+int check_history(const std::string& fen) {
+    constexpr const char* kStart = "rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/8/8/PPPPPPPP/RNBQKBNR w KQkq - 0 1";
+    forge::Searcher clean(16, 1);
+    const Result expected = search_fen(clean, fen, 14);
+    print_result("fresh", fen, expected);
+    if (!expected.ok || !forge::is_mate_score(expected.score)) {
+        std::cout << "history FAIL: fresh search did not prove a mate\n";
+        return 1;
+    }
+    forge::Searcher stained(16, 1);
+    const Result prelude = search_fen(stained, kStart, 10);
+    if (!prelude.ok) return 1;
+    // Drop the previous table only. History tables stay, which is the bug.
+    stained.clear_hash();
+    const Result after = search_fen(stained, fen, 14);
+    print_result("after-startpos", fen, after);
+    if (!same(expected, after)) {
+        std::cout << "history FAIL\n";
+        return 1;
+    }
+    std::cout << "history ok\n";
+    return 0;
+}
+
+int check_threads(const std::string& fen, bool use_nnue, int runs) {
+    forge::nnue::enabled = use_nnue;
+    forge::Searcher one(16, 1);
+    const Result expected = search_fen(one, fen, 14);
+    print_result(use_nnue ? "nnue-t1" : "t1", fen, expected);
+    if (!expected.ok) return 1;
+    if (!use_nnue && !forge::is_mate_score(expected.score)) {
+        std::cout << "threads FAIL: Threads 1 did not prove a mate\n";
+        return 1;
+    }
+    forge::Searcher two(16, 2);
+    int mismatches = 0;
+    Result first_mismatch{};
+    for (int i = 0; i < runs; ++i) {
+        two.clear();
+        const Result got = search_fen(two, fen, 14);
+        if (!same(expected, got)) {
+            if (mismatches == 0) first_mismatch = got;
+            ++mismatches;
+        }
+    }
+    std::cout << (use_nnue ? "nnue-threads2 " : "threads2 ") << fen << " runs " << runs
+              << " mismatches " << mismatches;
+    if (mismatches > 0) {
+        std::cout << " first " << score_text(first_mismatch.score) << " " << first_mismatch.move;
+    }
+    std::cout << "\n";
+    if (mismatches > 0) {
+        std::cout << "threads FAIL\n";
+        return 1;
+    }
+    std::cout << "threads ok\n";
+    return 0;
+}
+
+} // namespace
+
+int main() {
+    forge::nnue::enabled = false;
+    const char* positions[] = {
+        "4K3/k7/8/8/2R5/8/8/8 w - - 0 1",
+        "8/8/8/8/8/1R6/2k5/5K2 w - - 0 1",
+        "3k4/8/3K4/8/8/8/8/3R4 w - - 0 1",
+    };
+    int failures = 0;
+    for (const char* fen : positions) failures += check_history(fen);
+    for (const char* fen : positions) failures += check_threads(fen, false, 30);
+    failures += check_threads("4K3/k7/8/8/2R5/8/8/8 w - - 0 1", true, 20);
+    if (failures != 0) {
+        std::cout << "FAILED " << failures << "\n";
+        return 1;
+    }
+    std::cout << "ok\n";
+    return 0;
+}

+#include "forge/board.hpp"
+#include "forge/search.hpp"
+
+#include <cstdlib>
+#include <iostream>
+#include <string>
+#include <string_view>
+
+// `go nodes` used to keep the previous iteration's score and take a best move
+// from the iteration the limit cut off. The score and the move must be the
+// pair produced by the last iteration that actually finished.
+
+namespace {
+
+int g_failures = 0;
+
+struct Outcome {
+    int score = 0;
+    int depth = 0;
+    std::uint64_t nodes = 0;
+    std::string move;
+};
+
+Outcome search_fen(std::string_view fen, int depth, std::uint64_t nodes, bool use_nodes) {
+    forge::Board board;
+    if (!board.set_fen(fen)) {
+        std::cerr << "bad fen " << fen << std::endl;
+        std::exit(2);
+    }
+    forge::Searcher searcher(16, 1);
+    forge::SearchLimits limits;
+    if (use_nodes) {
+        limits.nodes = nodes;
+        limits.nodes_specified = true;
+        limits.depth = 32;
+    } else {
+        limits.depth = depth;
+    }
+    const forge::SearchInfo info =
+        searcher.search(board, limits, false, forge::Searcher::TTAccess::Exclusive);
+    Outcome out;
+    out.score = info.score;
+    out.depth = info.depth;
+    out.nodes = info.nodes;
+    out.move = info.best_move.is_none() ? "none" : forge::Board::move_to_uci(info.best_move);
+    return out;
+}
+
+void check_span(std::string_view fen) {
+    std::cout << "fen " << fen << std::endl;
+    Outcome previous = search_fen(fen, 1, 0, false);
+    std::cout << "depth 1 score " << previous.score << " move " << previous.move
+              << " nodes " << previous.nodes << std::endl;
+    bool saw_change = false;
+    for (int depth = 2; depth <= 8 && !saw_change; ++depth) {
+        const Outcome current = search_fen(fen, depth, 0, false);
+        std::cout << "depth " << depth << " score " << current.score << " move " << current.move
+                  << " nodes " << current.nodes << std::endl;
+        if (current.move == previous.move) {
+            previous = current;
+            continue;
+        }
+        saw_change = true;
+        std::cout << "span depth " << previous.depth << " nodes " << previous.nodes << " -> depth "
+                  << current.depth << " nodes " << current.nodes << std::endl;
+        if (current.nodes <= previous.nodes + 1) {
+            std::cout << "FAIL span too small" << std::endl;
+            ++g_failures;
+            return;
+        }
+        const std::uint64_t step = std::max<std::uint64_t>(1, (current.nodes - previous.nodes) / 8);
+        for (std::uint64_t budget = previous.nodes + 1; budget < current.nodes; budget += step) {
+            const Outcome limited = search_fen(fen, 0, budget, true);
+            if (limited.depth <= 0) {
+                std::cout << "nodes " << budget << " depth 0 score " << limited.score << " move "
+                          << limited.move << std::endl;
+                if (limited.score != 0) {
+                    std::cout << "FAIL unfinished search published a score" << std::endl;
+                    ++g_failures;
+                }
+                continue;
+            }
+            const Outcome finished = search_fen(fen, limited.depth, 0, false);
+            const bool match = limited.score == finished.score && limited.move == finished.move;
+            std::cout << "nodes " << budget << " depth " << limited.depth << " score " << limited.score
+                      << " move " << limited.move << " finished-score " << finished.score
+                      << " finished-move " << finished.move << (match ? " PASS" : " FAIL") << std::endl;
+            if (!match) ++g_failures;
+        }
+    }
+    if (!saw_change) {
+        std::cout << "FAIL no depth changed the best move" << std::endl;
+        ++g_failures;
+    }
+}
+
+} // namespace
+
+int main() {
+    check_span("rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/8/8/PPPPPPPP/RNBQKBNR w KQkq - 0 1");
+    check_span("8/8/8/8/4k3/8/3R4/4K3 w - - 0 1");
+    if (g_failures != 0) {
+        std::cout << "FAIL failures " << g_failures << std::endl;
+        return 1;
+    }
+    std::cout << "PASS fixed-node score and move agree" << std::endl;
+    return 0;
+}
`````

`````text
#include "forge/nnue.hpp"
#include "nnue_weights.inc"

#include <cstdint>
#include <fstream>
#include <iostream>
#include <string>

namespace {

void write_u32(std::ostream& out, std::uint32_t value) {
    const unsigned char bytes[4] = {
        static_cast<unsigned char>(value),
        static_cast<unsigned char>(value >> 8),
        static_cast<unsigned char>(value >> 16),
        static_cast<unsigned char>(value >> 24),
    };
    out.write(reinterpret_cast<const char*>(bytes), 4);
}

void write_i16(std::ostream& out, std::int16_t value) {
    const auto bits = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(value);
    const unsigned char bytes[2] = {
        static_cast<unsigned char>(bits),
        static_cast<unsigned char>(bits >> 8),
    };
    out.write(reinterpret_cast<const char*>(bytes), 2);
}

void write_i16s(std::ostream& out, const std::int16_t* data, std::size_t count) {
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < count; ++i) write_i16(out, data[i]);
}

} // namespace

int main(int argc, char** argv) {
    if (argc != 2) {
        std::cerr << "usage: nnue_convert <output>\n";
        return 2;
    }
    std::ofstream out(argv[1], std::ios::binary);
    if (!out) {
        std::cerr << "cannot write " << argv[1] << '\n';
        return 1;
    }
    out.write("FORGENET", 8);
    write_u32(out, 1);
    write_u32(out, static_cast<std::uint32_t>(forge::nnue::HiddenSize));
    write_i16s(out, NnueW1, sizeof(NnueW1) / sizeof(NnueW1[0]));
    write_i16s(out, NnueB1, sizeof(NnueB1) / sizeof(NnueB1[0]));
    write_i16s(out, NnueW2, sizeof(NnueW2) / sizeof(NnueW2[0]));
    write_i16(out, NnueB2);
    if (!out) {
        std::cerr << "write failed\n";
        return 1;
    }
    std::cout << "wrote " << argv[1] << " hidden " << forge::nnue::HiddenSize << '\n';
    return 0;
}
`````

`````text
#include "forge/board.hpp"
#include "forge/nnue.hpp"

#include <cstdint>
#include <fstream>
#include <iostream>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

namespace {

int failures = 0;

void expect(bool ok, const std::string& name) {
    if (ok) {
        std::cout << "ok " << name << '\n';
        return;
    }
    std::cout << "FAIL " << name << '\n';
    ++failures;
}

std::vector<unsigned char> read_file(const std::string& path) {
    std::ifstream input(path, std::ios::binary);
    input.seekg(0, std::ios::end);
    const auto length = input.tellg();
    input.seekg(0);
    std::vector<unsigned char> bytes(static_cast<std::size_t>(length));
    if (length > 0) input.read(reinterpret_cast<char*>(bytes.data()), length);
    return bytes;
}

void write_file(const std::string& path, const std::vector<unsigned char>& bytes) {
    std::ofstream output(path, std::ios::binary);
    output.write(reinterpret_cast<const char*>(bytes.data()), static_cast<std::streamsize>(bytes.size()));
}

int evaluate_fen(const char* fen) {
    forge::Board board;
    if (!board.set_fen(fen)) return 999999;
    forge::nnue::Accumulator accumulator;
    forge::nnue::refresh(board, accumulator);
    return forge::nnue::evaluate(board, accumulator);
}

} // namespace

int main(int argc, char** argv) {
    if (argc != 2) {
        std::cerr << "usage: nnue_file_test <lock-net>\n";
        return 2;
    }
    const std::string net_path = argv[1];
    const char* start = "rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/8/8/PPPPPPPP/RNBQKBNR w KQkq - 0 1";
    const char* kiwipete = "r3k2r/p1ppqpb1/bn2pnp1/3PN3/1p2P3/2N2Q1p/PPPBBPPP/R3K2R w KQkq - 0 1";
    const int start_builtin = evaluate_fen(start);
    const int kiwi_builtin = evaluate_fen(kiwipete);

    std::string error;
    const bool loaded = forge::nnue::load_file(net_path, error);
    expect(loaded && error.empty(), "load converted net");
    expect(evaluate_fen(start) == start_builtin, "startpos eval matches built-in net");
    expect(evaluate_fen(kiwipete) == kiwi_builtin, "kiwipete eval matches built-in net");

    std::vector<unsigned char> bytes = read_file(net_path);
    expect(bytes.size() > 16 && bytes.size() >= 8, "converted file is non-empty");

    auto shifted = bytes;
    const std::uint16_t bias = std::uint16_t(shifted[shifted.size() - 2]) |
                               (std::uint16_t(shifted[shifted.size() - 1]) << 8);
    const std::uint16_t bumped = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(bias + 2000);
    shifted[shifted.size() - 2] = static_cast<unsigned char>(bumped);
    shifted[shifted.size() - 1] = static_cast<unsigned char>(bumped >> 8);
    const std::string shifted_path = net_path + ".shifted";
    write_file(shifted_path, shifted);
    expect(forge::nnue::load_file(shifted_path, error), "load shifted bias");
    const bool changed = evaluate_fen(start) != start_builtin || evaluate_fen(kiwipete) != kiwi_builtin;
    expect(changed, "shifted bias changes an evaluation");

    expect(forge::nnue::load_file("", error) && error.empty(), "empty path restores built-in net");
    expect(evaluate_fen(start) == start_builtin && evaluate_fen(kiwipete) == kiwi_builtin,
           "restored eval matches built-in net");

    auto magic = bytes;
    magic[0] = 'X';
    write_file(net_path + ".magic", magic);
    expect(!forge::nnue::load_file(net_path + ".magic", error) && error == "nnue: bad magic",
           "bad magic keeps the current net");
    expect(evaluate_fen(start) == start_builtin, "eval unchanged after bad magic");

    auto version = bytes;
    version[8] = 2;
    write_file(net_path + ".version", version);
    expect(!forge::nnue::load_file(net_path + ".version", error) && error == "nnue: unsupported version",
           "wrong version keeps the current net");

    auto hidden = bytes;
    hidden[12] = 128;
    hidden[13] = 0;
    write_file(net_path + ".hidden", hidden);
    expect(!forge::nnue::load_file(net_path + ".hidden", error) && error == "nnue: wrong size",
           "wrong hidden size keeps the current net");

    auto truncated = bytes;
    truncated.pop_back();
    write_file(net_path + ".short", truncated);
    expect(!forge::nnue::load_file(net_path + ".short", error) && error == "nnue: wrong size",
           "truncated file keeps the current net");

    auto extra = bytes;
    extra.push_back(0);
    write_file(net_path + ".extra", extra);
    expect(!forge::nnue::load_file(net_path + ".extra", error) && error == "nnue: wrong size",
           "oversized file keeps the current net");

    expect(!forge::nnue::load_file(net_path + ".missing", error) && error == "nnue: cannot open file",
           "missing file keeps the current net");
    expect(evaluate_fen(start) == start_builtin && evaluate_fen(kiwipete) == kiwi_builtin,
           "eval unchanged after rejected files");

    if (failures != 0) {
        std::cout << failures << " failed\n";
        return 1;
    }
    std::cout << "PASS\n";
    return 0;
}
`````

`````text
let closed = false;
let stderr = '';
let bestmoves = 0;
let infoLines = 0;
let searches = 0;
let fatalError = null;
const closedPromise = new Promise(resolve => {
  engine.once('error', error => { fatalError = error; events.emit('failure', error); });
  engine.once('close', (code, signal) => {
    closed = true;
    console.log('PROCESS EXIT code=' + code + ' signal=' + signal);
    events.emit('failure', new Error('engine exited before awaited response'));
    resolve({ code, signal });
  });
});
engine.stderr.on('data', chunk => {
  stderr += chunk.toString();
  process.stdout.write('[engine stderr]\n' + chunk.toString());
});
readline.createInterface({ input: engine.stdout }).on('line', line => {
  console.log('< ' + line);
  if (line.startsWith('bestmove ')) ++bestmoves;
  if (line.startsWith('info depth ')) ++infoLines;
  events.emit('line', line);
});
function waitFor(predicate, milliseconds, description) {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    if (closed || fatalError) { reject(fatalError || new Error('engine already closed')); return; }
    const timer = setTimeout(() => finish(new Error('timeout waiting for ' + description)), milliseconds);
    const onLine = line => { if (predicate(line)) finish(null, line); };
    const onFailure = error => finish(error);
    function finish(error, line) {
      clearTimeout(timer);
      events.off('line', onLine);
      events.off('failure', onFailure);
      if (error) reject(error); else resolve(line);
    }
    events.on('line', onLine);
    events.on('failure', onFailure);
  });
}
function send(command) {
  console.log('> ' + command);
  engine.stdin.write(command + '\n');
}
function assert(condition, message) { if (!condition) throw new Error(message); }
async function main() {
  let reply = waitFor(line => line === 'uciok', 15000, 'uciok');
  send('uci');
  await reply;
  send('setoption name Threads value 1');
  send('setoption name Hash value 16');
  send('setoption name OwnBook value false');
  reply = waitFor(line => line === 'readyok', 15000, 'readyok');
  send('isready');
  await reply;
  for (const command of commands) {
    if (!command.startsWith('go ')) { send(command); continue; }
    const beforeBest = bestmoves;
    const beforeInfo = infoLines;
    const started = process.hrtime.bigint();
    const response = waitFor(line => line.startsWith('bestmove '), 10000, command + ' bestmove');
    response.catch(() => {});
    send(command);
    if (command.includes('3000000000')) {
      await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 150));
      assert(!closed, 'large-clock engine exited');
      assert(bestmoves === beforeBest, 'large clock returned bestmove before stop at 150 ms');
      assert(infoLines > beforeInfo, 'large-clock search produced no progress before 150 ms');
      console.log('CHECK still searching after 150 ms; no bestmove and search info observed');
      send('stop');
    }
    const best = await response;
    const elapsed = Number(process.hrtime.bigint() - started) / 1e6;
    assert(bestmoves === beforeBest + 1, 'expected exactly one bestmove');
    assert(!best.startsWith('bestmove 0000'), 'unexpected null bestmove in start position');
    if (command === 'go movetime +80') assert(elapsed >= 20, 'leading-plus clock returned too early: ' + elapsed + ' ms');
    if (!command.includes('3000000000')) assert(elapsed < 5000, 'finite/malformed clock did not finish promptly');
    ++searches;
    console.log('PASS search=' + searches + ' elapsed_ms=' + elapsed.toFixed(3) + ' command=' + JSON.stringify(command));
  }
  assert(searches === 7, 'expected seven source clock cases, got ' + searches);
  send('quit');
  engine.stdin.end();
  const exit = await closedPromise;
  assert(exit.code === 0 && exit.signal === null, 'engine did not exit cleanly');
  assert(!/AddressSanitizer|UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer|runtime error:|LeakSanitizer/.test(stderr), 'sanitizer report found');
  console.log('STDERR bytes=' + Buffer.byteLength(stderr));
  console.log('PASS all 7 clock UCI cases; no sanitizer report');
}
main().catch(async error => {
  console.error('FAIL ' + error.stack);
  if (!closed) engine.kill('SIGTERM');
  await closedPromise;
  process.exitCode = 1;
});
`````

`````text
// A legal position whose main-search capture picker stores more than 64
// SEE-losing captures. On the lock, that write runs past bad_captures_.
#include "forge/search.hpp"

#include <cstdlib>
#include <iostream>
#include <string>

namespace {

constexpr std::string_view Fen =
    "3r4/Pn1Q1p2/1Q1n1QpN/1p1Q1pRB/1Qbp1QpN/2bQ1pRB/3r1QpK/2k2q2 w - - 0 1";

int losing_captures(const forge::Board& board) {
    int count = 0;
    for (const forge::Move move : board.pseudo_legal_moves(true)) {
        if (!board.see_ge(move, 0)) ++count;
    }
    return count;
}

} // namespace

int main() {
    forge::Board board;
    std::string error;
    if (!board.set_fen(Fen, &error)) {
        std::cerr << "fen rejected: " << error << "\n";
        return 1;
    }
    const int losing = losing_captures(board);
    std::cout << "in_check " << (board.in_check() ? 1 : 0) << std::endl;
    std::cout << "losing_captures " << losing << std::endl;
    if (board.in_check() || losing <= 64) {
        std::cerr << "position does not force the 64-slot capture list\n";
        return 1;
    }

    forge::Searcher searcher(16, 1);
    forge::SearchLimits limits;
    limits.depth = 1;
    const forge::SearchInfo result = searcher.search(board, limits, false);
    if (result.best_move.is_none() || !board.is_legal(result.best_move)) {
        std::cerr << "search did not return a legal move\n";
        return 1;
    }
    std::cout << "bestmove " << forge::Board::move_to_uci(result.best_move) << "\n";
    std::cout << "nodes " << result.nodes << "\n";
    return 0;
}
`````

`````text
# UCI clock cases. Times are what the fixed engine does with
# Threads 1, Hash 16, OwnBook false, Move Overhead 10 (the default).
# The lock engine parses every one of these numbers as 0 and answers bestmove
# in about 1 ms.

# 3000000000 does not fit in a signed 32-bit int. The search must still be
# running 150 ms later. Stop it; do not wait out the clock.
position startpos
go wtime 3000000000 btime 3000000000

# A leading plus is 80 ms, not zero. The hard limit is 80 - overhead = 70 ms.
position startpos
go movetime +80

# A negative clock clamps to 0. The hard limit becomes 1 ms.
position startpos
go movetime -5

# A token that is not an integer is 0. The hard limit becomes 1 ms.
# A second sign and overflow with trailing junk are the same, not a huge clock.
position startpos
go movetime abc
go movetime +-80
go movetime 999999999999999999999abc

# Black to move uses btime. 3000000000 must not collapse to 0 just because
# it is the black clock. wtime 1 is white's clock and is ignored here.
position startpos moves e2e4
go wtime 1 btime 3000000000
`````

`````text
+ cat forge-combo29/tests_t3/clock_commands.txt
# UCI clock cases. Times are what the fixed engine does with
# Threads 1, Hash 16, OwnBook false, Move Overhead 10 (the default).
# The lock engine parses every one of these numbers as 0 and answers bestmove
# in about 1 ms.

# 3000000000 does not fit in a signed 32-bit int. The search must still be
# running 150 ms later. Stop it; do not wait out the clock.
position startpos
go wtime 3000000000 btime 3000000000

# A leading plus is 80 ms, not zero. The hard limit is 80 - overhead = 70 ms.
position startpos
go movetime +80

# A negative clock clamps to 0. The hard limit becomes 1 ms.
position startpos
go movetime -5

# A token that is not an integer is 0. The hard limit becomes 1 ms.
# A second sign and overflow with trailing junk are the same, not a huge clock.
position startpos
go movetime abc
go movetime +-80
go movetime 999999999999999999999abc

# Black to move uses btime. 3000000000 must not collapse to 0 just because
# it is the black clock. wtime 1 is white's clock and is ignored here.
position startpos moves e2e4
go wtime 1 btime 3000000000
`````

`````text
const fs = require('fs');
const { spawn } = require('child_process');
const { EventEmitter } = require('events');

const enginePath = process.env.FORGE_CLOCK_ENGINE || '/workspace/work/build-asan/forge';

  stdio: ['pipe', 'pipe', 'pipe']
});
const events = new EventEmitter();
let closed = false;
let stderr = '';
let bestmoves = 0;
let infoLines = 0;
let searches = 0;
let fatalError = null;
const closedPromise = new Promise(resolve => {
  engine.once('error', error => { fatalError = error; events.emit('failure', error); });
  engine.once('close', (code, signal) => {
    closed = true;
    console.log('PROCESS EXIT code=' + code + ' signal=' + signal);
    events.emit('failure', new Error('engine exited before awaited response'));
    resolve({ code, signal });
  });
});
engine.stderr.on('data', chunk => {
  stderr += chunk.toString();
  process.stdout.write('[engine stderr]\n' + chunk.toString());
});
readline.createInterface({ input: engine.stdout }).on('line', line => {
  console.log('< ' + line);
  if (line.startsWith('bestmove ')) ++bestmoves;
  if (line.startsWith('info depth ')) ++infoLines;
  events.emit('line', line);
});
function waitFor(predicate, milliseconds, description) {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    if (closed || fatalError) { reject(fatalError || new Error('engine already closed')); return; }
    const timer = setTimeout(() => finish(new Error('timeout waiting for ' + description)), milliseconds);
    const onLine = line => { if (predicate(line)) finish(null, line); };
    const onFailure = error => finish(error);
    function finish(error, line) {
      clearTimeout(timer);
      events.off('line', onLine);
      events.off('failure', onFailure);
      if (error) reject(error); else resolve(line);
    }
    events.on('line', onLine);
    events.on('failure', onFailure);
  });
}
function send(command) {
  console.log('> ' + command);
  engine.stdin.write(command + '\n');
}
function assert(condition, message) { if (!condition) throw new Error(message); }
async function main() {
  let reply = waitFor(line => line === 'uciok', 15000, 'uciok');
  send('uci');
  await reply;
  send('setoption name Threads value 1');
  send('setoption name Hash value 16');
  send('setoption name OwnBook value false');
  reply = waitFor(line => line === 'readyok', 15000, 'readyok');
  send('isready');
  await reply;
  for (const command of commands) {
    if (!command.startsWith('go ')) { send(command); continue; }
    const beforeBest = bestmoves;
    const beforeInfo = infoLines;
    const started = process.hrtime.bigint();
    const response = waitFor(line => line.startsWith('bestmove '), 10000, command + ' bestmove');
    response.catch(() => {});
    send(command);
    if (command.includes('3000000000')) {
      await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 150));
      assert(!closed, 'large-clock engine exited');
      assert(bestmoves === beforeBest, 'large clock returned bestmove before stop at 150 ms');
      assert(infoLines > beforeInfo, 'large-clock search produced no progress before 150 ms');
      console.log('CHECK still searching after 150 ms; no bestmove and search info observed');
      send('stop');
    }
    const best = await response;
    const elapsed = Number(process.hrtime.bigint() - started) / 1e6;
    assert(bestmoves === beforeBest + 1, 'expected exactly one bestmove');
    assert(!best.startsWith('bestmove 0000'), 'unexpected null bestmove in start position');
    if (command === 'go movetime +80') assert(elapsed >= 20, 'leading-plus clock returned too early: ' + elapsed + ' ms');
    if (!command.includes('3000000000')) assert(elapsed < 5000, 'finite/malformed clock did not finish promptly');
    ++searches;
    console.log('PASS search=' + searches + ' elapsed_ms=' + elapsed.toFixed(3) + ' command=' + JSON.stringify(command));
  }
  assert(searches === 7, 'expected seven source clock cases, got ' + searches);
  send('quit');
  engine.stdin.end();
  const exit = await closedPromise;
  assert(exit.code === 0 && exit.signal === null, 'engine did not exit cleanly');
  assert(!/AddressSanitizer|UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer|runtime error:|LeakSanitizer/.test(stderr), 'sanitizer report found');
  console.log('STDERR bytes=' + Buffer.byteLength(stderr));
  console.log('PASS all 7 clock UCI cases; no sanitizer report');
}
main().catch(async error => {
  console.error('FAIL ' + error.stack);
  if (!closed) engine.kill('SIGTERM');
  await closedPromise;
  process.exitCode = 1;
});
`````

Actual recorded output/transcript:

`````text
node <<'NODE'
const fs = require('fs');
const { spawn } = require('child_process');
const { EventEmitter } = require('events');
const readline = require('readline');
const enginePath = process.env.FORGE_CLOCK_ENGINE || '/workspace/work/build-asan/forge';
const commandPath = '/workspace/work/dwqww/forge-combo29/tests_t3/clock_commands.txt';
const commands = fs.readFileSync(commandPath, 'utf8').split(/\r?\n/).map(line => line.trim()).filter(line => line && !line.startsWith('#'));
console.log('ENGINE ' + enginePath);
console.log('COMMANDS ' + commandPath);
const engine = spawn(enginePath, [], {
  cwd: '/workspace/work/dwqww',
  env: { ...process.env, ASAN_OPTIONS: 'detect_leaks=1:halt_on_error=1', UBSAN_OPTIONS: 'halt_on_error=1:print_stacktrace=1' },
  stdio: ['pipe', 'pipe', 'pipe']
});
const events = new EventEmitter();
let closed = false;
let stderr = '';
let bestmoves = 0;
let infoLines = 0;
let searches = 0;
let fatalError = null;
const closedPromise = new Promise(resolve => {
  engine.once('error', error => { fatalError = error; events.emit('failure', error); });
  engine.once('close', (code, signal) => {
    closed = true;
    console.log('PROCESS EXIT code=' + code + ' signal=' + signal);
    events.emit('failure', new Error('engine exited before awaited response'));
    resolve({ code, signal });
  });
});
engine.stderr.on('data', chunk => {
  stderr += chunk.toString();
  process.stdout.write('[engine stderr]\n' + chunk.toString());
});
readline.createInterface({ input: engine.stdout }).on('line', line => {
  console.log('< ' + line);
  if (line.startsWith('bestmove ')) ++bestmoves;
  if (line.startsWith('info depth ')) ++infoLines;
  events.emit('line', line);
});
function waitFor(predicate, milliseconds, description) {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    if (closed || fatalError) { reject(fatalError || new Error('engine already closed')); return; }
    const timer = setTimeout(() => finish(new Error('timeout waiting for ' + description)), milliseconds);
    const onLine = line => { if (predicate(line)) finish(null, line); };
    const onFailure = error => finish(error);
    function finish(error, line) {
      clearTimeout(timer);
      events.off('line', onLine);
      events.off('failure', onFailure);
      if (error) reject(error); else resolve(line);
    }
    events.on('line', onLine);
    events.on('failure', onFailure);
  });
}
function send(command) {
  console.log('> ' + command);
  engine.stdin.write(command + '\n');
}
function assert(condition, message) { if (!condition) throw new Error(message); }
async function main() {
  let reply = waitFor(line => line === 'uciok', 15000, 'uciok');
  send('uci');
  await reply;
  send('setoption name Threads value 1');
  send('setoption name Hash value 16');
  send('setoption name OwnBook value false');
  reply = waitFor(line => line === 'readyok', 15000, 'readyok');
  send('isready');
  await reply;
  for (const command of commands) {
    if (!command.startsWith('go ')) { send(command); continue; }
    const beforeBest = bestmoves;
    const beforeInfo = infoLines;
    const started = process.hrtime.bigint();
    const response = waitFor(line => line.startsWith('bestmove '), 10000, command + ' bestmove');
    response.catch(() => {});
    send(command);
    if (command.includes('3000000000')) {
      await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 150));
      assert(!closed, 'large-clock engine exited');
      assert(bestmoves === beforeBest, 'large clock returned bestmove before stop at 150 ms');
      assert(infoLines > beforeInfo, 'large-clock search produced no progress before 150 ms');
      console.log('CHECK still searching after 150 ms; no bestmove and search info observed');
      send('stop');
    }
    const best = await response;
    const elapsed = Number(process.hrtime.bigint() - started) / 1e6;
    assert(bestmoves === beforeBest + 1, 'expected exactly one bestmove');
    assert(!best.startsWith('bestmove 0000'), 'unexpected null bestmove in start position');
    if (command === 'go movetime +80') assert(elapsed >= 20, 'leading-plus clock returned too early: ' + elapsed + ' ms');
    if (!command.includes('3000000000')) assert(elapsed < 5000, 'finite/malformed clock did not finish promptly');
    ++searches;
    console.log('PASS search=' + searches + ' elapsed_ms=' + elapsed.toFixed(3) + ' command=' + JSON.stringify(command));
  }
  assert(searches === 7, 'expected seven source clock cases, got ' + searches);
  send('quit');
  engine.stdin.end();
  const exit = await closedPromise;
  assert(exit.code === 0 && exit.signal === null, 'engine did not exit cleanly');
  assert(!/AddressSanitizer|UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer|runtime error:|LeakSanitizer/.test(stderr), 'sanitizer report found');
  console.log('STDERR bytes=' + Buffer.byteLength(stderr));
  console.log('PASS all 7 clock UCI cases; no sanitizer report');
}
main().catch(async error => {
  console.error('FAIL ' + error.stack);
  if (!closed) engine.kill('SIGTERM');
  await closedPromise;
  process.exitCode = 1;
});
NODE
`````

`````text
#include "forge/board.hpp"
#include "forge/nnue.hpp"

#include <cstdint>
#include <fstream>
#include <iostream>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

namespace {

int failures = 0;

void expect(bool ok, const std::string& name) {
    if (ok) {
        std::cout << "ok " << name << '\n';
        return;
    }
    std::cout << "FAIL " << name << '\n';
    ++failures;
}

std::vector<unsigned char> read_file(const std::string& path) {
    std::ifstream input(path, std::ios::binary);
    input.seekg(0, std::ios::end);
    const auto length = input.tellg();
    input.seekg(0);
    std::vector<unsigned char> bytes(static_cast<std::size_t>(length));
    if (length > 0) input.read(reinterpret_cast<char*>(bytes.data()), length);
    return bytes;
}

void write_file(const std::string& path, const std::vector<unsigned char>& bytes) {
    std::ofstream output(path, std::ios::binary);
    output.write(reinterpret_cast<const char*>(bytes.data()), static_cast<std::streamsize>(bytes.size()));
}

int evaluate_fen(const char* fen) {
    forge::Board board;
    if (!board.set_fen(fen)) return 999999;
    forge::nnue::Accumulator accumulator;
    forge::nnue::refresh(board, accumulator);
    return forge::nnue::evaluate(board, accumulator);
}

} // namespace

int main(int argc, char** argv) {
    if (argc != 2) {
        std::cerr << "usage: nnue_file_test <lock-net>\n";
        return 2;
    }
    const std::string net_path = argv[1];
    const char* start = "rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/8/8/PPPPPPPP/RNBQKBNR w KQkq - 0 1";
    const char* kiwipete = "r3k2r/p1ppqpb1/bn2pnp1/3PN3/1p2P3/2N2Q1p/PPPBBPPP/R3K2R w KQkq - 0 1";
    const int start_builtin = evaluate_fen(start);
    const int kiwi_builtin = evaluate_fen(kiwipete);

    std::string error;
    const bool loaded = forge::nnue::load_file(net_path, error);
    expect(loaded && error.empty(), "load converted net");
    expect(evaluate_fen(start) == start_builtin, "startpos eval matches built-in net");
    expect(evaluate_fen(kiwipete) == kiwi_builtin, "kiwipete eval matches built-in net");

    std::vector<unsigned char> bytes = read_file(net_path);
    expect(bytes.size() > 16 && bytes.size() >= 8, "converted file is non-empty");

    auto shifted = bytes;
    const std::uint16_t bias = std::uint16_t(shifted[shifted.size() - 2]) |
                               (std::uint16_t(shifted[shifted.size() - 1]) << 8);
    const std::uint16_t bumped = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(bias + 2000);
    shifted[shifted.size() - 2] = static_cast<unsigned char>(bumped);
    shifted[shifted.size() - 1] = static_cast<unsigned char>(bumped >> 8);
    const std::string shifted_path = net_path + ".shifted";
    write_file(shifted_path, shifted);
    expect(forge::nnue::load_file(shifted_path, error), "load shifted bias");
    const bool changed = evaluate_fen(start) != start_builtin || evaluate_fen(kiwipete) != kiwi_builtin;
    expect(changed, "shifted bias changes an evaluation");

    expect(forge::nnue::load_file("", error) && error.empty(), "empty path restores built-in net");
    expect(evaluate_fen(start) == start_builtin && evaluate_fen(kiwipete) == kiwi_builtin,
           "restored eval matches built-in net");

    auto magic = bytes;
    magic[0] = 'X';
    write_file(net_path + ".magic", magic);
    expect(!forge::nnue::load_file(net_path + ".magic", error) && error == "nnue: bad magic",
           "bad magic keeps the current net");
    expect(evaluate_fen(start) == start_builtin, "eval unchanged after bad magic");

    auto version = bytes;
    version[8] = 2;
    write_file(net_path + ".version", version);
    expect(!forge::nnue::load_file(net_path + ".version", error) && error == "nnue: unsupported version",
           "wrong version keeps the current net");

    auto hidden = bytes;
    hidden[12] = 128;
    hidden[13] = 0;
    write_file(net_path + ".hidden", hidden);
    expect(!forge::nnue::load_file(net_path + ".hidden", error) && error == "nnue: wrong size",
           "wrong hidden size keeps the current net");

    auto truncated = bytes;
    truncated.pop_back();
    write_file(net_path + ".short", truncated);
    expect(!forge::nnue::load_file(net_path + ".short", error) && error == "nnue: wrong size",
           "truncated file keeps the current net");

    auto extra = bytes;
    extra.push_back(0);
    write_file(net_path + ".extra", extra);
    expect(!forge::nnue::load_file(net_path + ".extra", error) && error == "nnue: wrong size",
           "oversized file keeps the current net");

    expect(!forge::nnue::load_file(net_path + ".missing", error) && error == "nnue: cannot open file",
           "missing file keeps the current net");
    expect(evaluate_fen(start) == start_builtin && evaluate_fen(kiwipete) == kiwi_builtin,
           "eval unchanged after rejected files");

    if (failures != 0) {
        std::cout << failures << " failed\n";
        return 1;
    }
    std::cout << "PASS\n";
    return 0;
}

int game_ply(const forge::Board& board) {

bool available() { return FORGE_HAS_NNUE != 0; }

bool load_file(std::string_view path, std::string& error) {
    error.clear();
    if (path.empty() || path == "<empty>") {
        live_weights() = make_builtin();
        return true;
    }
    const std::string name(path);
    std::ifstream input(name, std::ios::binary);
    if (!input) {
        error = "nnue: cannot open file";
        return false;
    }
    input.seekg(0, std::ios::end);
    const std::streamoff length = input.tellg();
    input.seekg(0);
    if (length < 0 || static_cast<std::uint64_t>(length) > 2U * 1024U * 1024U) {
        error = "nnue: wrong size";
        return false;
    }
    std::vector<unsigned char> bytes(static_cast<std::size_t>(length));
    if (length > 0) input.read(reinterpret_cast<char*>(bytes.data()), length);
    if (!input || static_cast<std::streamoff>(input.gcount()) != length) {
        error = "nnue: cannot open file";
        return false;
    }
    if (bytes.size() < 8) {
        error = "nnue: wrong size";
        return false;
    }
    if (std::memcmp(bytes.data(), "FORGENET", 8) != 0) {
        error = "nnue: bad magic";
        return false;
    }
    if (bytes.size() < 16) {
        error = "nnue: wrong size";
        return false;
    }
    if (read_u32(bytes.data() + 8) != 1U) {
        error = "nnue: unsupported version";
        return false;
    }
    const std::uint32_t hidden = read_u32(bytes.data() + 12);
    if (hidden != static_cast<std::uint32_t>(HiddenSize) || bytes.size() != kNetBytes) {
        error = "nnue: wrong size";
        return false;
    }
    std::vector<std::int16_t> w1(static_cast<std::size_t>(InputCount) * HiddenSize);
    std::vector<std::int16_t> b1(HiddenSize);
    std::vector<std::int16_t> w2(2 * HiddenSize);
    const unsigned char* cursor = bytes.data() + 16;
    auto take = [&cursor](std::vector<std::int16_t>& out) {
        for (std::int16_t& value : out) {
            value = read_i16(cursor);
            cursor += 2;
        }
    };
    take(w1);
    take(b1);
    take(w2);
    const std::int16_t b2 = read_i16(cursor);
    Weights incoming;
    quantize(incoming, w1.data(), b1.data(), w2.data(), b2);
    live_weights() = std::move(incoming);
    return true;
}
`````

`````text
# Fastchess

[![Fastchess](https://github.com/Disservin/fastchess/actions/workflows/fastchess.yml/badge.svg?branch=master)](https://github.com/Disservin/fastchess/actions/workflows/fastchess.yml)

Fastchess is a versatile command-line tool designed for running chess engine
tournaments.  
Written primarily in C++17, it utilizes [doctest](https://github.com/doctest/doctest) as its testing
framework.

With Fastchess, you can effortlessly orchestrate chess tournaments, configure
time controls, and execute matches concurrently for optimal time efficiency.
Extensively tested for high concurrency (with up to 250 threads) and
short time controls (0.2+0.002s), it exhibits minimal timeout issues, with only
10 matches out of 20,000 experiencing timeouts.

## What's New

- **Logging Changes**: Logs no longer include the engine output by default.
  You can enable this feature by adding `engine=true` to
  the log option.

- **UCI Compliance Checker**: Fastchess now offers a built-in UCI compliance checker,  
  allowing you to verify that engines adhere to the UCI protocol.  
  To use this feature, simply run the following command:
  `./fastchess --compliance ENGINE_PATH [ENGINE_ARGS]`
- **Enhanced Cutechess Output**: The Cutechess output support has been refined to
  enhance compatibility with other tools. Simply switch the `-output` option to
  cutechess to enable it.
- **Extended PGN Data**: You can now track nodes, seldepth, nps (nodes per
  second), hashfull, tbhits, and time left in the PGN output. Refer to the `-pgnout`
  option for detailed information.
- **Quick Match Option**: We've introduced a `-quick` option for running quick
  matches between two engines with a specified book. Specify
  `-quick cmd=ENGINE1 cmd=ENGINE2 book=BOOK` to swiftly initiate a match.

- **GZIP Compression for logs**: The logs can now be compressed using GZIP to
  reduce disk space usage. You can enable this feature adding `ZLIB=true` to
  the `make` command and the enabling the `compress=true` option for the log.
  **Compiling with ZLIB=true will include _gzstream_ a wrapper for zlib from**  
  **Deepak Bandyopadhyay and Lutz Kettner, which is licensed under LGPL.**

## Quick start

### Building from source

Building Fastchess from source is straightforward. Just follow these steps:

1. Clone the repository `git clone https://github.com/Disservin/fastchess.git`
2. Navigate to the Fastchess directory `cd fastchess`
3. Build the executable `make -j` for GCC and `make -j CXX=clang++` for Clang (requires GCC >= 7.3.0 or Clang >= 8.0.0).

The executable will be located in the root directory.

If you are on Linux, you can run `make install` to install the binary on your system.  
By default, the installation prefix is set to `/usr/local`. You can change this location by specifying the PREFIX during installation. The binary will be installed in `$(PREFIX)/bin`, and the man page will be installed in `$(PREFIX)/share/man/man1`.

```bash
make install PREFIX=/custom/path
```

This will install the binary in /custom/path/bin and the man page in /custom/path/share/man/man1. If PREFIX is not specified, it defaults to /usr/local.

### Download the latest release

Prefer a pre-compiled version?

Download the latest release from our [release page](https://github.com/Disservin/fastchess/releases).

Current dev versions are available as artifacts from the [CI](https://github.com/Disservin/fastchess/actions?query=is%3Asuccess+event%3Apush+branch%3Amaster).

### Example usage

Here's an example of how to use Fastchess:

```bash
fastchess.exe -engine cmd=Engine1.exe name=Engine1 -engine cmd=Engine2.exe
name=Engine2 -each tc=10+0.1 -rounds 200 -repeat -concurrency 4
```

_Note: It is highly encouraged to use an opening book._

## Command line options

See [man.md](man.md) for a detailed description of all command line options.

## Contributing

We welcome contributions to fastchess! Please ensure that any changes you make
are **beneficial** to the development and **pass the CI tests**.

The code follows the Google style and is formatted with clang-format. When
creating pull requests, please format your code accordingly.

To contribute, you'll need a recent GCC compiler that supports C++17 and the
ability to run the Makefile. You can locally test your changes by running
`make -j tests`, followed by executing the `./fastchess-tests` executable to
verify your changes pass the tests.

You can format the code with clang-format by running `make format`.
After making changes to the man file, you need to run `make update-man`.

Maintainers can find the release procedure in [RELEASE.md](RELEASE.md).

## Maintainers & contributors

The following people have push access to the repository:

- [Disservin](https://github.com/Disservin)
- [Szil](https://github.com/SzilBalazs)
- [PGG106](https://github.com/PGG106)

Special thanks to [gahtan-syarif](https://github.com/gahtan-syarif) for his many contributions and
thorough testing.
PREFIX ?= /usr/local
BINDIR = $(PREFIX)/bin
MANDIR = $(PREFIX)/share/man/man1
MANPAGE_SOURCE = man.md  # Path to the markdown file for the man page
MANPAGE_OUTPUT = fastchess.1

ifeq ($(shell uname), Linux)
	LOWDOWN_INSTALLED := $(shell command -v lowdown >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo yes || echo no)
endif

all: ## Build the project
	@echo "Building.."
	$(MAKE) -C app BINARY_PATH=../
	@echo "Done."

tests: ## Run tests
	@echo "Running tests.."
	$(MAKE) -C app tests BINARY_PATH=../
	@echo "Done."

coverage: ## Run tests with coverage
	@echo "Running tests with coverage.."
	$(MAKE) -C app coverage BINARY_PATH=../
	@echo "Done."

scan:
	@echo "Running scan-build.."
	$(MAKE) -C app scan=yes BINARY_PATH=../
	@echo "Done."

install: ## Install the binary and man page
	@echo "Installing fastchess binary to: $(DESTDIR)$(BINDIR)"
	@install -d $(DESTDIR)$(BINDIR)
	@install fastchess $(DESTDIR)$(BINDIR)
	@if [ "$(shell uname)" = "Linux" ] && [ "$(LOWDOWN_INSTALLED)" = "no" ]; then \
		printf "\033[33mWarning: 'lowdown' is not installed. Man page will not be generated.\033[0m\n"; \
	else \
		make install-manpage --no-print-directory ; \
	fi
	@echo "Done."

manpage: ## Generate the man page from Markdown using lowdown
	@lowdown -s -Tman -o  $(MANPAGE_OUTPUT) $(MANPAGE_SOURCE) -mtitle="Fastchess"

install-manpage: manpage ## Install the man page to $(MANDIR)
	@install -d $(DESTDIR)$(MANDIR)
	@install -m 644 $(MANPAGE_OUTPUT) $(DESTDIR)$(MANDIR)
	@echo "Installed man page."

update-man: ## Update man like page
	lowdown -Tterm man.md > fastchess-tmp-man-page
	xxd -i fastchess-tmp-man-page | sed 's/fastchess_tmp_man_page/man/g' | sed 's/fastchess_tmp_man_page_len/man_len/g' | sed 's/unsigned char/inline unsigned char/g' | sed 's/unsigned int/inline unsigned int/g' > temp.hpp
	printf '/* Generate with make update-man*/\n#pragma once\n' > ./app/src/cli/man.hpp
	echo 'namespace fastchess::man {' >> ./app/src/cli/man.hpp
	cat temp.hpp >> ./app/src/cli/man.hpp
	echo '}' >> ./app/src/cli/man.hpp
	rm temp.hpp
	clang-format -i ./app/src/cli/man.hpp
	rm fastchess-tmp-man-page

update-fmt: ## Fetch subtree fmt
	@echo "Updating fmt.."
	git fetch https://github.com/fmtlib/fmt.git main
	git subtree pull --prefix=app/third_party/fmt https://github.com/fmtlib/fmt.git main --squash
	@echo "Done."

format: ## Format code
	@echo "Formatting.."
	$(MAKE) -C app format
	@echo "Done."

tidy: ## Check clang-tidy
	@echo "Checking includes.."
	$(MAKE) -C app tidy
	@echo "Done."

clean: ## Clean up
	@echo "Cleaning up.."
	$(MAKE) -C app clean BINARY_PATH=../
	@echo "Done."

help: ## Print this help
	@egrep -h '\s##\s' $(MAKEFILE_LIST) | awk 'BEGIN {FS = ":.*?## "}; {printf "\033[36m  %-30s\033[0m %s\n", $$1, $$2}'

.PHONY: all tests install manpage install-manpage update-man clean format update-fmt help coverage
```

# NAME

fastchess - a command-line tool for managing chess games with engines

# SYNOPSIS

fastchess [OPTIONS]

# DESCRIPTION

Fastchess is a command-line tool designed to manage and orchestrate chess games between engines. It provides a range of options to configure game settings, engine parameters, concurrency, and output formats.

# OPTIONS

The following options are available. Options are grouped by their primary function for easier navigation.
The default values are the first value in parentheses.

## General & Help

`-version`   
Print `fastchess` version number and exit.

`-help`   
Print this help message and exit.

## Tournament Setup

`-quick cmd=ENGINE1 cmd=ENGINE2 book=BOOK`   
Shortcut for predefined game settings involving two engines, time controls, rounds, and concurrency.

`-concurrency (1|N)`   
Play N games concurrently, limited by the number of hardware threads. Default value is 1.

`-force-concurrency`   
Ignore the hardware concurrency limit and force the specified concurrency.

`-rounds (2|N)`   
Play N rounds of games where each game within the round uses the same opening. Default value is 2.

`-games (2|N)`   
Play N games in each round. Default value is 2. Setting this higher than 2 does not provide meaningful results.

`-repeat`   
Set the number of games to 2. Equivalent to `-games 2`.

`-sprt elo0=ELO0 elo1=ELO1 alpha=ALPHA beta=BETA model=(normalized|logistic|bayesian)`   
Set parameters for a Sequential Probability Ratio Test (SPRT).

- `model`:
    - `normalized` - Uses nElo (default).
    - `logistic` - Uses regular/logistic Elo.
    - `bayesian` - Uses BayesElo.

`-tournament (roundrobin|gauntlet)`   
Choose type of tournament.

- `roundrobin` - each engine plays every other engine (default)
- `gauntlet` - the first `-seeds` engines play against all other engines

`-seeds (1|N)`   
First N engines are playing the `gauntlet`. Default value is 1.

`-variant (standard|fischerandom)`   
Choose between the following game variants:

- `standard` - play Standard Chess (default)
- `fischerandom` - play Fischer Random Chess

`-noswap`   
Prevent swapping of colors.

`-reverse`   
Use a tournament schedule with reversed colors.

`-wait (0|N)`   
Wait N milliseconds between games. Default is 0.

## Engine Configuration

`-each OPTIONS`   
Apply specified OPTIONS to both engines.

`-engine OPTIONS`   
Apply specified OPTIONS to the next engine.

- `cmd=COMMAND` - Specify engine command.
- `name=NAME` - Set engine name. If not specified, the executable's filename would be used.
- `args="ARGS"` - Pass multiple arguments using args="ARG1 ARG2".
- `tc=moves/minutes:seconds+increment` - Time control in Cute-Chess format.
- `timemargin=N` - Time margin for exceeding time limit.
- `st=N` - Movetime in seconds.
- `nodes=N` - Max number of nodes to search.
- `restart=(off|on)` - Enable or disable engine restarts between games, default is off.
- `plies=N` - Max number of plies (depth) to search. The alias `depth` can also be used.
- `proto=uci` - Specify the engine protocol. Only `uci` is supported.
- `dir=DIRECTORY` - Working directory for the engine.
- `option.name=VALUE` - Set engine-specific options. The value for a button option should be "true" or "false".

## Adjudication & Rules

`-draw movenumber=(0|N) movecount=(1|N) score=(0|N)`   
Enables draw adjudication based on number of moves, move count, and score threshold.

- `movenumber` - number of moves before checking for a draw. Default is 0.
- `movecount` - number of consecutive moves below the score threshold. Default is 1.
- `score` - score threshold (in centipawns) for a draw. Default is 0.

`-resign movecount=(1|N) score=(0|N) [twosided=(false|true)]`   
Configures engine resignation based on move count and score threshold.

- `movecount` - number of consecutive moves above the score threshold. Default is 1.
- `score` - score threshold (in centipawns) to resign. Default is 0.
- `twosided` - if true, enables two-sided resignation. Defaults to false.

`-maxmoves N`   
Enables draw adjudication if the game reaches N moves without a result.

`-tb PATHS`   
Adjudicate games using Syzygy tablebases. PATHS must be a semicolon-separated (on Windows) or colon-separated (other platforms)
list of paths to the tablebase directories.
Only the WDL tablebase files are required.

`-tbpieces N`   
Only use tablebase adjudication for positions with N pieces or less.

`-tbignore50`   
Disable the fifty move rule for tablebase adjudication.

`-tbadjudicate (BOTH|WIN_LOSS|DRAW)`   
Control when tablebase adjudication is applied. SETTING can be:
- `BOTH` - Adjudicate both wins and draws (default)
- `WIN_LOSS` - Only adjudicate won/lost positions
- `DRAW` - Only adjudicate drawn positions

## Opening Book Management

`-openings file=NAME format=(epd|pgn) [order=(sequential|random)] [plies=(Max plies|N)] [start=(1|N)]`   
Specifies an opening book file and its format for game starting positions.

- `format` - file format, either epd or pgn.
- `order` - order of openings (`random` or `sequential`). Default is `sequential`.
- `plies` - number of plies for pgn. Defaults to max available plies.
- `start` - starting index of the opening book. Default is 1.

`-srand SEED`   
Specify the seed for opening book randomization.

## Output & Reporting

`-output format=(fastchess|cutechess)`   
Choose the output format for game results (`fastchess` or `cutechess`). Default is `fastchess`.

**`-pgnout [file=NAME] [notation=(san|lan|uci)] [append=(true|false)] [nodes=(false|true)] [seldepth=(false|true)] [nps=(false|true)] [hashfull=(false|true)] [tbhits=(false|true)] [pv=(false|true)] [timeleft=(false|true)] [latency=(false|true)] [min=(false|true)] [match_line=REGEX]`**  
Export games in PGN format with specified notations and optional tracking of nodes, seldepth, and others.

- `notation`:

    - `san` - Standard Algebraic Notation (default)
    - `lan` - Long Algebraic Notation
    - `uci` - Universal Chess Interface

- `file` - Specify filename. Default is `fastchess_(date)_(time).pgn`.
- `append` - Append to file. Default is true.
- `nodes` - Track node count. Default is false.
- `seldepth` - Track seldepth. Default is false.
- `nps` - Track nps. Default is false.
- `hashfull` - Track hashfull. Default is false.
- `tbhits` - Track tbhits. Default is false.
- `pv` - Track the full pv. Default is false.
- `timeleft` - Track time left at end of move. Default is false.
- `latency` - Track difference between measured time and engine reported time at end of move. Default is false.
- `min` - Minimal PGN format. Default is false.
- `match_line` - Add lines to the PGN that match the given regex.

**`-epdout [file=NAME] [append=(true|false)]`**  
Export the final position of each game in EPD format.

- `file` - Specify filename. Default is `fastchess_(date)_(time).epd`.
- `append` - Append to file. Default is true.

`-event NAME`   
Set the event name for the PGN header.

`-site NAME`   
Set the site name for the PGN header.

`-ratinginterval (10|N)`   
Set rating interval for the report. Default is 10. Set to 0 to disable.

`-scoreinterval (1|N)`   
For cutechess output, set interval for printing score results. Default is 1.

`-report penta=(true|false)`   
Reports pentanomial statistics (for Fastchess output). Defaults to true.

## Persistence & Recovery

`-config [file=NAME] [discard=(false|true)] [outname=(config.json|NAME)] [stats=(true|false)]`   
Load engine configurations to resume games from previous sessions.

- `file` - the file name to load the configuration from.
- `discard` - discard the loaded configuration after loading. Defaults to false. This lets you specify a filename to save the
  configuration to, while ignoring it for the current session.
- `outname` - the auto-generated file name of the config. Default is "config.json".
- `stats` - load the stats from the config file, and ignore `append=false` for `-pgnout` and `-epdout`. Defaults to true.

`-recover`   
Enables crash recovery to attempt to recover the engine after a crash and continue the tournament.

`-autosaveinterval (20|N)`   
Automatically saves the tournament state every N games. Default is 20. Set to 0 to disable.

## Testing & Debugging

`--compliance ENGINE_PATH [ARGS]`   
Check the UCI compliance of an engine by running it with the specified arguments.

`-crc32 pgn=true`   
Calculate the CRC32 checksum for the PGN file.

**`-check-mate-pvs`**  
Check that PVs for mate scores have the correct length and end in checkmate.

`-show-latency`   
Show the "think" latency (difference between measured and reported time) for each engine.
Note that a lot of engines add 1ms to the time they report, so the latency will be 1ms higher than the actual latency.
It is also possible that the latency is negative, due to different measurement methods or missing synchronization of the clocks
between different threads.

**`-testEnv`**  
Specifies that the program is running in a test environment (OpenBench/Fishtest). This will change some outputs/settings.

**`-strict`**  
Makes fastchess exit and return 1 on any warning.

**`-log file=NAME level=(warn|trace|info|err|fatal) append=(true|false) compress=(false|true) realtime=(true|false) engine=(false|true)`**  
Specify a log file with a specific log level.
Set append to false to overwrite existing file. Default is true.
Set compress to true to write to gzipped file with timestamp (ignores append). Default is false.
By default engine logs are disabled. Set engine to true to enable them.

- LEVEL:
    - `trace`
    - `info`
    - `warn` (default)
    - `err`
    - `fatal`

**`-events file=(NAME|-) info=(false|true) interval=MS`**  
Write a machine-readable event stream, one JSON object per line (NDJSON), to NAME or to stdout with `file=-`.
On stdout, event lines always start with `{"event":`, which normal output never does.
Events are written and flushed by a separate thread, so a slow reader never stalls games.
The option is not saved into the config file. When it is enabled, PGN games also get a `[GameId "N"]` tag.
Events: `tournament_started` (with `schema`), `game_started`, `move`, `thinking` (only with `info=true`,
at most one every `interval` ms per game, default 250), `game_finished`, `game_aborted` and `tournament_finished`.
Times are in milliseconds, moves are in UCI notation, and scores are `{"cp":N}` or `{"mate":N}` from White's point of view.

`-use-affinity [CPUS]`   
Enable thread affinity for binding engines to CPU cores.

- CPUS - The cpus to use as a list of the form "3,5,7-11,13".

`-startup-ms N`   
Set the maximum time to wait for engine UCI initialization in milliseconds. Default is 10000.

`-ucinewgame-ms N`   
Set the maximum time to wait for engine UCI new game initialization in milliseconds. Default is 60000.

`-ping-ms N`   
Set the maximum time to wait for engine ping responses in milliseconds, this is everything else which doesn't fit the above categories. Default is 60000.


# EXAMPLES

To start a match between two engines using random openings from book.epd:

```sh
$ fastchess -engine cmd=Engine1.exe name=Engine1 -engine cmd=Engine2.exe \
  name=Engine2 -openings file=book.epd format=epd order=random \
  -each tc=60+0.6 option.Hash=64 -rounds 200 -repeat -concurrency 4
```

NAME

    fastchess - a command-line tool for managing chess games with engines

    Play N games concurrently, limited by the number of hardware threads.
    Default value is 1.

    -force-concurrency
    Ignore the hardware concurrency limit and force the specified
    concurrency.

    than 2 does not provide meaningful results.
`````

`````text
  const startFen = 'rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/8/8/PPPPPPPP/RNBQKBNR w KQkq - 0 1';
  let eventCount = 0, moveCount = 0, aborted = 0;
  for await (const line of readline.createInterface({input: fs.createReadStream(folder + '/events.ndjson')})) {
    if (!line.trim()) continue;
    const e = JSON.parse(line); eventCount++;
    if (e.event === 'tournament_started' || e.event === 'tournament_finished') tournaments.push(e);
    if (e.event === 'game_started') {
      if (starts.has(e.game)) errors.push('duplicate start ' + e.game);
      starts.set(e.game, e);
      if (e.start_fen !== startFen || e.opening.length !== 0) errors.push('not plain start ' + e.game);
    }
    if (e.event === 'move') {
      moveCount++;
      moves.set(e.game, (moves.get(e.game) || 0) + 1);
      if (e.legal !== true) illegal.push(e);
    }
    if (e.event === 'game_aborted') { aborted++; abnormal.push(e); }
    if (e.event === 'game_finished') {
      if (finishes.has(e.game)) errors.push('duplicate finish ' + e.game);
      finishes.set(e.game, e);
      if (e.termination !== 'normal') abnormal.push(e);
    }
  }
  const wld = {wins:0, losses:0, draws:0}, reasons = {};
  for (const [id, e] of finishes) {
    const s = starts.get(id);
    if (!s) { errors.push('missing start ' + id); continue; }
    if ((moves.get(id) || 0) !== e.plies) errors.push('event ply count mismatch ' + id);
    reasons[e.reason] = (reasons[e.reason] || 0) + 1;
    if (e.result === '1/2-1/2') wld.draws++;
    else if (e.result === '1-0' || e.result === '0-1') {
      const winner = e.result === '1-0' ? s.white : s.black;
      if (winner === 'integration') wld.wins++; else if (winner === 'lock') wld.losses++; else errors.push('unknown winner ' + id);
    } else errors.push('unfinished result ' + id + ': ' + e.result);
  }
  for (let id=1; id<=400; id++) if (!starts.has(id) || !finishes.has(id)) errors.push('missing game ' + id);
  const pgnText = fs.readFileSync(folder + '/games.pgn','utf8');
  const games = pgnText.split(/(?=^\[Event )/m).filter(x => x.trim());
  const pgnIds = new Set(), pgnWld = {wins:0,losses:0,draws:0};
  for (const game of games) {
    const tags = Object.fromEntries([...game.matchAll(/^\[(\w+) "([^"]*)"\]$/gm)].map(m => [m[1],m[2]]));
    const id = Number(tags.GameId), s = starts.get(id), e = finishes.get(id);
    if (pgnIds.has(id)) errors.push('duplicate PGN game ' + id);
    pgnIds.add(id);
    if (!s || !e || tags.White !== s.white || tags.Black !== s.black || tags.Result !== e.result || tags.Termination !== e.termination || Number(tags.PlyCount) !== e.plies) errors.push('PGN/event mismatch ' + id);
    if (!game.trimEnd().endsWith(tags.Result)) errors.push('PGN movetext result mismatch ' + id);
    if (tags.Result === '1/2-1/2') pgnWld.draws++;
    else if ((tags.Result === '1-0' && tags.White === 'integration') || (tags.Result === '0-1' && tags.Black === 'integration')) pgnWld.wins++;
    else pgnWld.losses++;
  }
  const traceFindings = [], inputGo = {}, optionCommands = {};
  let traceLines = 0;
  for await (const line of readline.createInterface({input: fs.createReadStream(folder + '/engine-trace.log')})) {
    traceLines++;
    if (/\b(crash|crashed|illegal|disconnect|disconnected|abnormal|forfeit|stalled|timeout|timed out)\b/i.test(line) || /^\[(WARN|ERROR|FATAL)/.test(line)) traceFindings.push({line:traceLines,text:line});
    const m = line.match(/\[Engine\].*?\s(integration|lock)\s+<--- (.*)$/);
    if (!m) continue;
    if (m[2].startsWith('go ')) {
      inputGo[m[1]] = (inputGo[m[1]] || 0) + 1;
      if (m[2] !== 'go nodes 20000') errors.push('unexpected search command: ' + line);
    }
    if (m[2].startsWith('setoption ')) optionCommands[m[1] + ': ' + m[2]] = (optionCommands[m[1] + ': ' + m[2]] || 0) + 1;
  }
  const consoleLines = fs.readFileSync(folder + '/console.txt','utf8').split('\n');
  const consoleWarnings = consoleLines.filter(x => /warning|error|fatal|crash|illegal|disconnect|abnormal|forfeit|stalled|timeout/i.test(x));
  if (starts.size !== 400 || finishes.size !== 400 || games.length !== 400 || pgnIds.size !== 400) errors.push('game count not 400');
  if (JSON.stringify(wld) !== JSON.stringify(pgnWld)) errors.push('W/L/D mismatch');
  if (!tournaments.some(e => e.event === 'tournament_finished')) errors.push('missing tournament_finished');
  const summary = {eventCount,starts:starts.size,finishes:finishes.size,pgnGames:games.length,moveCount,illegalMoves:illegal.length,abortedGames:aborted,abnormalTerminations:abnormal.length,integration:wld,pgnIntegration:pgnWld,reasons,inputGo,optionCommands,consoleWarnings,traceFindings,errors,tournaments};
  fs.writeFileSync(folder + '/audit-summary.json',JSON.stringify(summary,null,2)+'\n');
  console.log(JSON.stringify(summary,null,2));
  if (illegal.length || abnormal.length || traceFindings.length || errors.length) process.exitCode = 1;
})().catch(e => {console.error(e); process.exitCode=1;});
`````
